title: refactor(ui): the 2D and 3D pages draw through the form seam
body:
**Stacked on #4220** (the multi-axis slice, which is stacked on #4218, the turning slice). The three slices change the same rows of the raw-call guard. Until they merge, this diff also shows their commits (42ca7bfc5, 9886fef31). The commit of this PR is b852d7257. After each parent merges, I merge `main` into this branch.

## What changed

The 2D and 3D page families of #1122 draw through the form seam.

- **Families.**
  - 2D (20 files): the 2D milling pages and the cutting pages, with the editors that they share. These are `mill2d_page`, `mill2d_more_page`, `trochoid_page`, `vcarve_page`, `probe_page`, `plasma_page`, `waterjet_page`, `wire_page`, `sinker_page`, `sinker_pick_rows`, `deburr_page`, `pockets_page`, `approach_page`, `predrilled_page`, `rest_pocket_page`, `start_exit_rows`, `pass_start_row`, `load_field`, `lead_page` and `kind_editors`.
  - 3D: `mill3d_page` and `undercut_page`. They had no raw call on `main`, so this family is one guard row only.
  - The common operation tabs (`heights_page`, `feeds_page`, `op_page`, `pages`) are not in a family of the #655 list. They stay outside the guard for a later slice.
- **New seam helpers** (`layout/controls.rs`). Each one is a thin wrapper that draws what the raw call drew:
  - `button_enabled` and `small_button_enabled`: a greyed-out button;
  - `checkbox`: a box that is not a property row (the start and exit group headers);
  - `list_row_truncated`: a list row with an ellipsis (a picked edge);
  - `note`: a dimmed line that wraps ("Not taken - ...");
  - `drag_row` and `drag_sized_row`: a configured `DragValue` in a `prop_row`, at its own width or at `CTRL_W`. `fields::int_range_row` now draws through `drag_row`.
- **The raw calls.** About 35 calls in 8 files go through these helpers, or through `list_row`, `button`, `small_button`, `int_range_row` and `text_row`.
- **Accessible names and the focus ring.** Seven fields now join the pane's Tab / Enter ring (#2516) and have their row's accessible name (#1119): Tab count, Taper angle, Vectors, Turns, EDM condition, Number of passes and Optimal load. Nothing else changes in what the user sees.
- **The guard** (`layout/form_seam_tests.rs`) gets the 2D and 3D families at 0. It now joins a line that starts with `.` to the line before it, so a call that rustfmt splits after `ui` counts. `deburr_page.rs` had one such call (`ui` / `.add_enabled(`), which the old line count did not see.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1122-form-seam-2d.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::layout::form_seam_tests::pages_do_not_add_raw_egui_calls_outside_the_form_seam`: the 2D and 3D families have 0 raw calls.
- `egui_app::layout::form_seam_tests::form_seam_guard_covers_only_the_migrated_families`: five families, each at 0.
- `egui_app::layout::form_seam_tests::the_guard_counts_a_raw_call_split_over_two_lines` (new): a split call counts, and a comment line does not.
- `egui_app::layout::form_seam_tests::the_2d_seam_helpers_keep_clicks_text_and_names` (new):
  - a greyed-out button and a greyed-out small button take no click;
  - an enabled button takes one click;
  - the check box toggles;
  - the note and the cut list row keep their text;
  - `drag_row` and `drag_sized_row` fields have their row's name.
- The page suites that cover the changed rows stay green: `wire_page_tests`, `sinker_machine_tests`, `sinker_pick_rows_tests`, `start_exit_tests`, `turning_start_exit_tests`, `tests::radial_step_field` and `pockets_tests`. All are in the `ui suites: lib` step.

No new test binary (#3187). The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by two.

## Screenshots

The Wire Contour page, from the off-screen renderer (`egui_kittest` with the headless wgpu device) at 620 x 1400, cropped to the top 540 px.
- The Passes tab has one skim added, tabs on and the tab count stated. It shows the skim buttons (greyed-out Move up and Move down), Add skim, Tab count and Add tab position.
- The Geometry tab shows the start and exit group headers and Taper angle.

A pixel comparison of the full frames gives 0 different pixels on both tabs. The images are on the images-only `pr-screenshots` branch of the fork.

|---|---|---|
| Passes | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/1122-2d/before-wire-passes.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/1122-2d/after-wire-passes.png) |
| Geometry | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/1122-2d/before-wire-geometry.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/1122-2d/after-wire-geometry.png) |

## Gates

On b852d7257:

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 10 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (2.5 min). It includes `ui suites: lib` (107 s) and the `boundary`, `sinker_setup` and `waterjet_tool` suites.

title: fix(rest): simulate the program ahead in the generation job, not at staging
body:
## What changed

A rest operation no longer simulates the program ahead while it is staged. The staging runs on the session thread (MCP) or the UI thread (GUI). The simulation now runs in the generation job, on the worker thread.

- `rest::prior_state` is split in two halves.
- `rest::stage_prior` does all world reads: the chain of operations ahead, the digest and the stock grid. It keeps the order and the refusals of before.
- `StagedPrior::simulate` cuts the cached moves ahead into the stock. It reads no world.
- `collect_job` keeps the staged half in the new field `GenJob::prior_staged`.
- `run_job` calls `GenJob::settle_prior` first. Thus the simulation runs on the job thread.
- The corner-relief reader (`zones_for_op`) settles the grid before its WCS yaw turn reads it.
- `prior_state` keeps its signature. It calls the two halves in sequence.

This covers 3D Pocket, Multi-Axis Rough, and a 2D Pocket or 2D Adaptive whose rest reads the previous operations.

## Cause

PR #3860 moved the generator of an MCP `generate` to a worker thread. But `StagedGeneration::new` calls `collect_job` on the session thread. For a rest operation, `collect_job` called `rest::prior_state`, which simulated all operations ahead. On a large part, this blocked every other MCP call for that time. The issue comment of 2026-11-24 names this open part.

## Tests

- Pin: `generate_staged::a_rest_reading_pocket_simulates_the_program_ahead_in_its_job_not_at_staging`.
  - It stages a 3D Pocket after a Face cut. It asserts that the staging thread simulates nothing.
  - It finishes the job on a second thread and asserts one simulation there.
  - It asserts that the path is equal to the path of the one-shot `GenerateOperation`.
- Red before the fix: `assertion left == right failed: staging simulates nothing; left: 1, right: 0`.
- Mutation: the simulation put back inside `stage` (the old timing) makes the pin red with the same message. With the fix restored, the pin is green.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green, 181 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (25.4 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Example catalog suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: 46 passed, 0 failed (4 ignored by their own markers).
- Light lane `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed.

## Goldens moved

None. The change moves where the simulation runs, not what it computes. The example catalog suites ran green, and `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples/catalog` is empty.

## Not exercised

- The original QA mould core project is not on this machine. I did not measure the time on it.
- A carried chain across setups (#318) stays eager on the staging thread. Its body comes from a per-thread cache. `docs/decisions/3035-rest-staging-worker.md` gives the reason.
- The stock grid is still built at staging (`first_held` needs the world). It is an allocation, not a simulation.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P3` PR (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").
- No UI change, so no screenshots.

## Open on #3035

- The run time of the generators on the mould core.
- A cancel point inside the generators.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs` or `crates/app/src/rest.rs`.

Changelog: A rest operation (3D Pocket, Multi-Axis Rough, rest 2D Pocket or 2D Adaptive) simulates the operations ahead in its background job, so MCP calls and the GUI stay responsive while it is staged.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3035#issuecomment-7200445799

Refs #3035

title: fix(adaptive): read the bore's star cell through offset rounding noise
body:
## What changed

- `adaptive::star::Star::new` cleans each opened row loop before the star laws read it. The new function `denoised` drops a vertex that is less than 1e-5 mm from the last vertex kept.
- The bore pin `BORE_PIN` in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs` moves to `(1642, 1614, 300)`. The old pin stays as `BORE_PIN_BEFORE_4010`, and each platform pin test rejects it. The unmeasured-platform band is centred on the new pin with the same half-widths.
- New fixture: `crates/motion/tests/fixtures/bore_z15_center.txt`. It holds the Z 15 center area of the user's bore (328 vertices), recorded from the 3-D ladder.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/4010-bore-level-plan.md`.

## Cause

The Z 15 and Z 5 levels give the planner a 328-vertex disc outline. The opening of this outline at R2.5 keeps 20 edges that are 1 or 2 Clipper units long (1.4e-6 to 2.2e-6 mm). Integer rounding turns each of these edges back about the pole.

- `radial` reads such an edge as a shadow.
- `disc_in_kernel` reads the line of the edge as a wall through the area.

So the star cell was refused and the growth rings planned the disc. The 128-vertex outline of Z 10 and Z 0 has no such edges, so those levels kept the morph spiral. A probe in the planner showed this on each level:

- 328 points: row 0 fails, so the growth rings plan it (`Grown::Done`).
- 128 points: a star cell, so the morph spiral plans it.

## Readings (macOS arm64, release)

| Level | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Z 15, Z 5 | 1933 planar feeds, 918 arcs, 999.92 mm | 410 planar feeds, 78 arcs, 330.07 mm |
| Z 10, Z 0 | 397 planar feeds, 72 arcs, 334.31 mm | no change |
| Whole path | (4688, 4660, 1980) | (1642, 1614, 300) |

Z 15 and Z 5 now reach the wall at y -7.498 (before: 0.153 mm short in -Y). The path verifies clean with no fallback and no budget note. On unchanged upstream main `498382c8e`, macOS read `(4688, 4660, 1980)`. This is the same triple that Windows and Linux read.

## Tests

- Pins (in `camcraft-motion` lib, `machining2d::adaptive::tests`):
  - `the_users_z15_bore_is_one_star_cell`
  - `the_users_z15_bore_plans_the_short_spiral` (the walk is less than 500 mm, it does not cross itself, and the rest is under `HSM_REST_MAX`)
- Red before the fix: yes. Both failed on unchanged code with "the bore's walk is 1146.46 mm". The note was the same plan-B corner note, at (5.30, -5.30).
- Mutation: I put back `star.rs` from `upstream/main`, and the two pins went red. I restored the fix, and the two pins went green.
- `pocket3d_hsm` in release with `--include-ignored`: the bore test and all the pin and band tests pass. `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level` fails at its `known-fail #1950` assert line, as it did before.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base 498382c8e`: 172 steps, 0 failed. This includes `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base 498382c8e`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. The example catalog suites ran green in the quick gate, and no `*.nc`, `*.cl` or catalog file changed. Only the count pin of `pocket3d_hsm` changed, as given above.

## Not exercised

- Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64 are not measured after the fix. Before the fix they read the same triple as macOS, so the pin follows the macOS reading. Their next run confirms it or adds a platform triple.
- No full heavy lanes. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a `P3` PR no heavy step. I ran the targeted heavy bore test in release (given above).
- No probe of the reading before the PR #3802 mesh (Z 10 on the long plan). I expect the same cause, but I did not check it.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/` or `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`.

Changelog: HSM Adaptive no longer cuts a round 3D Pocket level with a plan three times too long when the outline has offset rounding noise (the bore levels now take the short spiral).

Fixes #4010

body:

## What changed

The last family of #1120: the window chrome inks. After this PR, each colour literal at a draw site in `crates/ui/src` reads a token, and the colour-literal guard has only permanent rows.

- Two colour tokens join `Tokens`. Each is also a theme-file key (`colors.<name>`):

title: fix(post): refuse a preset above the machine's last preset row
body:
Stacked on #4164 (merge #4164 first).

## What changed

- A machine file can state a new optional key, `controller.work_offset_max`. It is the highest work offset that the control holds. On a Heidenhain control it is the last row of the preset table.
- The machine reader and the raw post engine refuse a value that is not a whole number from 1 to 255. The message names the key.
- The key is an installation fact, the same as `tooling.max_tool_number` (#4164). The mirror carries it.
- The post engine refuses a `PARAM WorkOffset` above the key. The refusal names the setup and the key. It comes before any script hook runs, so it applies to each post.
- `fehlmann-picomax55.mch` states `"work_offset_max": 5`. Its description tells the shop to check the preset table at the control.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- A machine without the key keeps the post's own limit. A key above the post's own limit does not raise that limit.

## Cause

- Both Heidenhain posts accept presets 1..6 (`workOffsetMax = 6`).
- The Picomax preset table on the 2008 delivery CD (`PRESET.PR`) has rows 0..5 only (`docs/research/heidenhain/picomax-55-review.md`, defect 14).
- `Q339=+6` names a row that does not exist. The control stops with an alarm.
- The machine file had no place to state the row count.

The refusal is a hard error, not a counted warning. A counted warning was not enough: the Klartext post throws "missing or unsupported preset (WorkOffset)" when the engine holds back the offset, and that error hid the warning.

## Tests

Pins, in the `heidenhain_cycles` directory suite (new submodule `heidenhain_cycles/preset_rows.rs`, no new test binary):

- `preset_rows::heidenhain_posts_refuse_a_preset_above_the_machine_preset_table`: preset 5 posts with no warning, and preset 6 is refused with `setup Setup1: uses work offset 6` and `controller.work_offset_max`. It runs both posts on the raw file and on the parsed mirror.
- `preset_rows::an_unstated_or_larger_machine_maximum_keeps_the_post_limit`: no machine posts preset 6; a key of 99 posts preset 6 and refuses 7 with "work offsets 1-6 only".
- `preset_rows::a_malformed_work_offset_max_is_refused_by_name`: 0, -1, 2.5, "5" and 256 are refused by the reader and by the raw engine.

Red before the fix: yes. On the unchanged code the test did not compile (no `Machine::work_offset_max`). With the two field assertions taken out, all three tests failed: preset 6 posted, and no value was refused.

Mutations (each one red, then restored and green):

- Engine guard disabled: `heidenhain_posts_refuse_a_preset_above_the_machine_preset_table` red.
- Mirror line disabled: the same test red (mirrored input).
- Reader range widened to 256: `a_malformed_work_offset_max_is_refused_by_name` red.

Gate on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `9d6ebbd62`: 343 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.3 min). The plan included each app suite that reads `heidenhain.cps`, `klartext_builtin`, `machine_controller` and the example catalog suites.
- Then a clippy fix (`b3541f715`, the guard as one `if let`). `cargo xtask gate quick --base HEAD~1` on the final head: 13 steps, 0 failed. It ran `post suites: lib`, `work_offset_index`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and the first-part suites.
- `cargo xtask gate test preset_rows --crate post --binary heidenhain_cycles` on the final head: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The light lane was not run. Its dry run shows only the motion adaptive and pocket twins. This diff does not change them.

## Goldens moved

None. The example catalog suites and the quick plan ran green. `git diff --stat` against #4164's head shows no `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` change.

## Not exercised

- The row count was not checked at the control. The value 5 comes from the 2008 CD. The issue's first "Done means" item stays with the maintainer. If the shop added rows, raise the key in the machine file.
- The setup's work offset list in the UI still offers offsets up to the post's limit. The post refusal blocks the wrong program. Display is a possible follow-up.
- An older app reads a project from this build and drops the key (no `deny_unknown_fields` on `Machine`), so it keeps the post's own limit. This is the same as for #4164.
- No UI change, so no screenshots.
- No heavy step: this is a `P3` PR (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

## Overlaps

- #4164: same lines (`FACT_KEYS`, the `Machine` fields, `parse_mch_with`, `checked_input`, `mirror`). This PR is stacked on it.
- #4161: touches `def.rs`, `parse.rs` and `machine_installation.rs`, in other fields and functions. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3982: touches `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, another section. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: A machine file can state `controller.work_offset_max`, the last preset row of the control; the post refuses a higher work offset by setup name, and the Fehlmann Picomax 55 states 5.

title: feat(tools): document component table and undoable assembly commands
body:
## What changed

The document now holds shared tool components, and each tool can hold a component stack. A change to one shared component updates each tool that uses it, in one undo step.

- `crates/app/src/schema.rs`: two new schema components.
  - `DocumentComponents` is a world singleton. It has one row (`DocumentComponent`) for each component id. A row keeps the #3642 `ToolComponent` and the #3643 `ComponentGeometry` together.
  - `ToolAssembly` sits on a tool entity. It is the stack: for each node, a component id and its `Mount`.
- `crates/app/src/tool_assembly.rs`: reads and writes the table and the stacks, lists the users of a component (`users_of`), and derives a tool (`derive`) with the #3643 resolver.
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_assembly.rs`: four undoable commands (below).
- `ChangeTool::assembled`: every `ChangeTool` law, with the body law judged against the body that lands in the same step.
- `DeleteTool` keeps the stack and restores it on undo. It moved to `commands/tool_delete.rs`, so that `commands/tool.rs` stays under 400 lines.
- Review fix 1: the generic `DeleteEntity` (the tree's delete) also restores the stack on undo. The two delete paths now snapshot and land one shared list, `ToolRecords` (`commands/tool_delete.rs`): the record, the number, the body, the cutter and the stack. A search found no other path that deletes a tool and restores it (the tool import's replace mode uses `DeleteTool`).
- The project loader clears the table, so that no row of the previous document leaks into the next one.
- Review fix 2: `NewDocument` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`) clears the table too, next to the units, machine and post resets.
- `camcraft_app` re-exports `component`, `component_geometry` and `connection_code` of `camcraft_tools`, so that a caller outside `app` can make a table row. This adds no crate dependency.

## The commands and their refusals

| Command | Does | Refuses by name |
|---|---|---|
| `UpsertDocumentComponent` | Adds a row. A held id goes through `EditDocumentComponent`. | Each edit refusal, for a held id. |
| `EditDocumentComponent` | Replaces a row. Derives each tool that uses it again. Lands the table, each `ToolDef` and each `ToolBody` in one undo step. | An id that the document does not hold; an edit equal to the row; each `derive` or `ChangeTool` refusal of any user tool, with the component id and the tool name. Nothing changes. |
| `DeleteDocumentComponent` | Deletes an unused row. | An unknown id; a used component (names the tools). |
| `SetToolAssembly` (`new`, `clear`) | Sets a stack and lands the derived records in one undo step. `clear` removes the stack and keeps the records. | No such tool; an unknown component id; each #3642 fit and #3643 resolver refusal; a body in the flutes; each `ChangeTool` law; a lathe-held tool. |

Operations go Stale by their stamps: the tool record and `tool_body::digest` are in each stamp. No command writes a status.

## Readings

- An insert edit from `CCMT09T304` to `CCMT09T308` changes the corner radius of the Ø25 and the Ø32 cutters from 0.4 mm to 0.8 mm. The diameters stay 25 mm and 32 mm. The two Face operations go Stale.
- A `DCMT11T304` in the CC seats is refused: `the edit of tool component 'insert-cc' is refused: tool 'Fly25': assembly: ... does not fit ...`.

## Pinning tests

In `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/assembly_cmds.rs` (joins the `tool_library_holders` suite):

- `one_shared_insert_edit_updates_two_assemblies_in_one_undo_step`
- `an_edit_one_assembly_cannot_take_is_refused_whole_by_name`
- `a_used_component_is_not_deleted_and_an_unused_one_is`
- `an_incompatible_stack_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
- `set_tool_assembly_lands_the_derived_tool_and_body_in_one_undo_step`
- `a_deleted_tool_comes_back_with_its_stack`
- `review_generic_delete_undo_keeps_assembly` (review fix 1: delete through `DeleteEntity`, undo, the stack is back, and a shared edit updates the tool again)

In `crates/ui/tests/machine.rs` (next to `new_document_retires_the_machine_with_the_rest`):

- `new_document_clears_the_component_table` (review fix 2)

The two review pins fail on `7ce62c040` and pass on the new head.

## Not exercised

- The turning insert of the issue. The resolver has only the spindle side (#3643 is open for the lathe side). The tests use a milling insert in two indexable cutters. `derive` refuses a lathe-held tool by name.
- A solid cutting item through the commands. The resolver pins of #3643 cover it, and `derive` uses the solid tool's own record.

## What is left

- #3645: the table and the stacks in `.camproj` and `.camtools`, the user library, `library_ref`. Today the derived `ToolDef` and the drawn body save; the stack and the table do not.
- #3647: the MCP tools for the four commands (`MCP: <command>` follow-up). This PR adds no MCP tool.
- #3648: the UI. It also decides how a hand edit (`ChangeTool`, `SetToolBody`) and a stack live together. Today the next component edit derives the records again.
- #3646: the full `Tool` record of a multi-seat cutter. Today an insert gives the diameter and the corner radius only.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3644-component-commands.md`.

## Gate

All on the final head `8fd0a47ec3519947a09f3ca78c650b882ff72d05` (log: first line is the head SHA):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 304 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The plan includes `app suites: tool_library_holders` (16 passed), `ui suites: machine` (8 passed) and `example_catalog`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The two review pins fail on `7ce62c040` (source fix held back, tests kept) and pass on the new head.

P6: no heavy step.

An edit of one component updates every tool that uses it in one undo step, and their operations go Stale. A delete of a used component and a stack that does not fit are refused by name.

title: fix(pocket3d): start and exit picks for 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

This is slice 3 of #3329: the 3D Pocket only. The 3D Pocket now takes a start point and an exit point. Its capability is the existing `PickCapability::Region` (the descent place of the first pass, and the end of the last pass). The picks seat the passes that the strategy already planned on each level. They never re-order the passes.

- Motion: `crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_seam.rs` (the seat laws and the refusals), `level_columns.rs` (the exact column law), `picked.rs` (`pocket3d_picked`, the plain or offset-shell ladder with "Do not touch" items, seated). The ladder gets one `picks` argument; each old caller passes `None`.
- `ladder.rs` gets smaller (441 lines, was 444): `mask_center` moves to `rest.rs`, unchanged.
- App: `OpType::Pocket3D => PickCapability::Region`; the 3D Pocket arm of `generate` calls `pocket3d_picked` only when a pick is set; `pick_kinds` refuses a pick under Adaptive and with Rest roughing; the MCP `edit_operation` schema names the region kind.

The title uses `fix`, because the issue has the `bug` label.

### Behaviour

- **Start:** on each level, the first ring of the first pass starts at its point nearest the start point. It cuts its whole lap back to that point. Then it runs on along its own cut, in its own direction, to its old start. From there the level is the automatic path, move for move: no link changes.
- **Start on zigzag rows:** an open row chain starts at its end nearest the start point (the chain runs the other way). Rows cut both ways, so the reversed chain cuts the same mix.
- **Exit:** on each level, the last ring of the last pass laps from its own start as before. Then it runs on along its own cut to its point nearest the exit point. An open zigzag chain ends at its end nearest the exit point. The operation's exit is the end of the last pass of the last level that cuts.
- **A level of one ring with the two picks:** the lap from the start point runs on straight to the exit point.
- A run-on re-traces a cut at the same depth. It removes no new material.
- The descent at the new start goes through the ladder's own entry rule (helix, ramp, arc, plunge and their stand-ins).
- The ladder reads the X and Y of a pick. A pick with a Z gets one note (`PICK_Z_UNREAD`).
- A ring of a ring strategy is never reversed (climb would become conventional cutting). The passes are never re-ordered (the ring order is the engagement law).
- With no pick, the output is the automatic path, byte for byte.

### Refusals (by name, never moved)

- A start point farther than 1.5 tool diameters from the start of the first pass of a level: `start point (x, y): the first pass of the 3D Pocket at Z z starts at (...), d mm from it, farther than the L mm ...`.
- A descent that the entry rule puts farther than that reach from the start point: `start point (x, y): the entry rule at Z z finds no room for its motion at the start point and descends at (...)`.
- An exit point farther than that reach from the end of the operation: `exit point (x, y): the last pass of the 3D Pocket at Z z ends at (...)`.
- A pick on a level that the Adaptive (HSM) plan spirals (its own entry bore and proved arcs).
- In the application, at the edit: a pick under the Adaptive strategy, and a pick with Rest roughing on.
- A plunge or retract column at a point that a pick moved that comes within the tool radius (less 0.01 mm) of the part.
  - The check is exact: each facet is clipped to the half-space above the column's foot, then `stock_sim::dist_seg_tri` measures the distance from the column's axis segment to what is left. There is no sampling. A distance that is not a number is a hit.
  - The moved points: the new start of a re-seated ring, the new end of a run-on, both ends of a reversed chain, and the descent place that the entry rule chose.
  - The islands law of the ladder already keeps each ring point clear above its level, so no ladder fixture reaches this refusal. It is a second, independent check, pinned by a unit test.

### Same-region rule

The start and the exit act on different passes of a level: the first pass and the last pass. Where a level has one pass, the two picks act on one ring: the lap from the start point runs on to the exit point (a re-trace, simple and safe). Where that one pass is an open chain, the exit is not moved: the exit reach law then refuses an exit that the chain does not end near.

### Mutation table

Each mutation was applied alone, then `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib level_seam` and `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pocket3d_pass_start picks` ran (M11: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test start_exit_shared pocket3d`).

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | No column law (`columns` checks no point) | RED: `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot` |
| M2 | Column law tests only the two ends of the column (no segment distance) | RED: `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot` |
| M3 | No start reach law | RED: `a_start_beyond_the_first_pass_is_refused_with_its_level`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | No exit reach law | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | No descent law | RED: `a_descent_far_from_the_start_point_is_refused`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M6 | No one-ring run-on from the start to the exit | RED: `a_level_of_one_ring_laps_from_the_start_and_runs_on_to_the_exit` |
| M7 | No run back to the old start after the re-seat | RED: `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends` |
| M8 | No exit run-on | RED: `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends`, `an_exit_pick_ends_the_operation_on_the_last_ring` |
| M9 | No zigzag reversal | RED: `zigzag_rows_start_at_their_end_nearest_the_start_point`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M10 | No refusal of an HSM level | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M11 | No application refusal (Adaptive, Rest roughing) | RED: `pocket3d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` |

## Readings

- Motion fixture (40 mm square pocket, 10 mm island, tool radius 3, Waterline, plunge entry, Z 8 / 3 / 0): a start at (30, 33) gives the descent of each level at (30, 32.2); the automatic descent is at (32.2, 32.2). An exit at (20, 11) gives the last cut end at (20, 12, 0), and the rise is straight up.
- Zigzag, 39.62 mm pocket, no island: a start at (38, 38) reverses the row chain; each level descends within 1 mm of (36.61, 36.61) (automatic: near (3.01, 3.01)).
- App brick (10 mm block in 40 x 40 stock, `EM-0600-4FL`, Offset rings, Z 6 / 2): a start at (-14, 10) gives each descent at (-12.961, 11.095) (automatic: (-12.636, 11.502)). An exit at (10, -21) gives the last cut end at (10, -19.99, 2).
- Reach with the 6 mm mill: 9 mm.

## Pinning tests

`camcraft-motion`, `tests/pocket3d_pass_start.rs`, new module `pocket3d_pass_start/picks.rs` (joins the existing suite, no new test binary):
- `no_pick_is_the_automatic_ladder_byte_for_byte` (Waterline, Offset rings, Zigzag, Auto; plain and offset shell)

Each picked path is gouge-checked at every cut move, sampled each 0.25 mm along its length (the island, the footprint, the floor). Each also cuts all that the automatic path cuts, level by level (a 0.5 mm grid of the swept tool disc).

title: fix(post): guard LinuxCNC preview measure check and catch spaced comment keywords
body:
Guard the LinuxCNC probe tolerance check with the task parameter `#<_task> EQ 1`.
In backplot preview, probe values are simulated or zero. The check stops the
preview with M2 when `#<_task>` is not checked. With this guard, the preview
continues and shows the toolpath. The tolerance check still stops the machine during
live execution when `#<_task>` is 1.

Ignore whitespace within keywords when checking comment strings against active keywords.
Add PYRELOAD to the active keyword regular expression. LinuxCNC accepts keywords
with spaces and lower-case letters. The comment guard preserves keyword boundaries
for arguments like file names and prefixes active comments with a dash to keep them inert.
Plain text like Message and Python stays unchanged.

Reason for new test binary:
- `crates/post/tests/linuxcnc_post.rs`: Dedicated integration suite for LinuxCNC post processor output, safety blocks, and comment guards against the JS engine.

Readings:
- LinuxCNC G-code Reference (Messages, Comments, Named Parameters #<_task>)

- `crates/post/tests/linuxcnc_post.rs`:
  - `probe_measure_check_guarded_by_task_parameter`
  - `active_comment_guard_catches_spaced_keywords_and_pyreload`

What was not exercised:
- Hardware execution on a physical CNC machine running LinuxCNC.

Changelog: LinuxCNC post guards probe measure check in preview mode and catches active comment keywords with spaces and PYRELOAD.

title: fix(gate): report skipped GPU tests and actual adapters
body:
## What changed

The gate keeps successful libtest output with `--show-output`. It reports each named GPU skip in the step summary. A successful process with incomplete GPU coverage has a `SKIP` row, not an `ok` row. Missing adapters use `SKIPPED (no adapter): <test>`. Other GPU refusals remain distinct.

The adapter report names the device that wgpu returned. It includes the backend and device type. CPU devices report software. Integrated and discrete GPUs report hardware. Virtual and other devices report unknown hardware identity.

The decision keeps the post-merge policy at "skip, but report". This change does not alter workflows, runners, adapter selection, kernels, parity assertions, tolerances or CPU fallback behavior.

## Verification

Final head: `99858f35ba6a42a7744804a2d9e76984bf2db3df`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: PASS. Both selected steps ran: GPU library tests and xtask unit tests.
- `cargo test -p xtask gpu_reporting`: PASS. The tests cover captured parallel output, mixed CPU passes and GPU skips, deduplication, adapter identity, unknown identity, and failure reporting.
- The new reporting tests failed before the fix. The captured-output test also failed without `--show-output`.
- `cargo xtask gate test the_gpu_cut_onto_a_keyframe_matches_the_cpu_law_or_skips_by_name --crate camcraft-gpu --binary cut_onto --exact`: PASS on software `llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8, 256 bits)` via Vulkan, device type Cpu.
- A process-scoped Vulkan-disabled probe ran the same parity test on hardware `Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 (CFL GT2)` via Gl, device type IntegratedGpu. This is evidence for this one small test on this host, not general hardware coverage.
- With process-scoped `VK_DRIVER_FILES=/nonexistent __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES=/nonexistent DISPLAY= WAYLAND_DISPLAY=`, the same gate printed a named `SKIPPED (no adapter)` and a `SKIP` row. Its exit code was zero under the existing skip policy.
- Adding `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` to that absent-adapter probe produced `FAIL` and exit code 1, as expected.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- Strict xtask clippy fails on the unchanged `clippy::needless_bool` in `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67`. This failure was reproduced before the edits. `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::needless_bool`: PASS. No source lint allowance was added.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.

## Limits and process

The light dry-run selects unrelated motion/app release builds and six steps. Those steps were not run for this reporting-only change. No full workspace, release, catalog or GUI build ran. Synthetic fixtures do not establish hardware parity. No maintainer runner or workflow was started. `graphify` is not installed on this host.

The first quick invocation reached the xtask tests but exceeded a 180-second tool timeout. The later full quick runs completed successfully. This timeout is not presented as a pass.

No scout was commissioned. Bounded direct discovery inspected `xtask/src/exec.rs`, `direct.rs`, `budget.rs`, `tests.rs`, the GPU adapter and shared harness, and equivalent skip diagnostics. No compute or safety algorithm changed. The existing `gpu_render` local cache emits its diagnostic only at initial device creation; this change reports diagnostics that the harness emits, not inferred skips from tests with no diagnostic.

Effort: medium

Process change: yes

Changelog: The gate reports named GPU skips and the actual adapter instead of hiding missing coverage behind a successful process exit.

Fixes #3879

title: feat(tools): lathe tool assemblies — nose-centre tip, orientation and clearance
body:
This PR is the lathe slice of #3643. It is pure domain code in `camcraft-tools`. It adds no crate edge, no ECS code and no file I/O.

## What changed

- New `crates/tools/src/lathe_assembly.rs` (with `lathe_assembly_error.rs`). `resolve_lathe` resolves a turning holder or a boring bar, its insert and its adapters to these values:
  - the nose centre as the tip of the turning frame (a `LathePlacement`, so the current lathe body path reads it without change);
  - the CRP in the turning frame;
  - the orientation (LinuxCNC 1-8): derived from the root coupling (rectangular shank = OD, round shank = boring bar), the seat hand and the insert shape (round = neutral), or stated by the caller;
  - the nose radius, the approach angle, the hand, the insert corner angle, the clearance angle and the inscribed circle;
  - one `LatheClearance` over the bodies of all components except the insert.
- The CRP is the insert's cutting point (its CIP, else its seat frame). We define it as the control point of the orientation chart: the point where the nose tangents parallel to X and Z meet. The nose centre is `CRP - r * tip_offset(q)` in the turning frame.
- `LatheBody` is a set of boxes or a mesh in the frame of the component. A revolved body on a lathe component is refused by name. It is never dropped.
- `LatheStation` states which root directions are radial and along the spindle (`RADIAL_SHANK`, `AXIAL_SHANK`).
- `tool_assembly::placed` (new, `pub(crate)`) holds the chain steps that `resolve` had before the gauge length. `resolve` calls it now. The lathe resolver gets the same #3642 fit refusals, port refusals, cycle refusals and frame refusals.
- `lathe_insert_zone::clip_axis` is now `pub(crate)`. The edge check uses it.
- Decision: a lathe section in `docs/decisions/3643-tool-assemblies.md`.

## Named refusals

- every refusal of the component chain (for example a CNMG09 in a PCLNR..12 seat: fit property `size`);
- a cutting item that is not an insert;
- an insert with no nose radius (a sharp corner or a wiper facet);
- a stated orientation that is not 1 to 8;
- a root coupling that does not show OD or ID (VDI, BMT, custom): "state the orientation";
- a bad station (a zero direction, directions that are not square);
- a revolved body on a lathe component;
- a holder body past the cutting lines of the insert, within one insert (25.4 mm) of the nose. This catches a wrong hand, a wrong stated orientation or a wrong seat frame. The window is clipped exactly, so a large facet with its corners outside the window is checked too;
- each `LatheClearance` refusal, on the bodies of the whole stack (the size cap and `MAX_TIP_GAP`).

## Readings

- CNMG120408 in PCLNR2525M12 (l1 = 150 mm, f1 = 32 mm): orientation 2 (derived), nose radius 0.8 mm, approach 95 degrees, insert angle 80 degrees, clearance 0 degrees, IC 12.7 mm. The nose centre is 0.8 mm up the radial and 0.8 mm along the spindle from the CRP. The CRP maps to (-0.8, 0, -0.8).
- Boring bar (25 mm, 200 mm long) in a VDI40 sleeve, orientation 3 stated: nose centre at (16.2, 0, -260.2) in the root frame. The bands end at z = 260.2 mm (the sleeve is in them). The sleeve alone gives `TipAway`. The stack passes.

## Pinning tests (`crates/tools/src/lathe_assembly_tests.rs`, in the tools lib)

- `a_cnmg_in_a_pclnr_has_its_nose_centre_at_the_tip`
- `the_derived_values_equal_todays_tool_record_and_placed_mesh_body` (equivalence pin: the same holder placed by hand on the current mesh path gives the same bands within 1e-9; the nose radius and the orientation equal a `Tool` of kind Turning with `lathe_orientation()`)
- `the_clearance_envelope_encloses_the_holder`
- `the_insert_plate_is_left_out_of_the_bands`
- `hand_and_shape_give_the_orientation_and_a_stated_one_wins` (PCLNL = 1, SRDCN + RCMT = 6)
- `a_boring_bar_in_a_sleeve_is_judged_as_one_body` (also a bar turned 180 degrees by `z_rot_deg`: refused)
- `a_mismatch_a_wrong_hand_and_degenerate_input_are_refused_by_name`

## Mutations (each one ran on winbuild, each one is red)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| the box body shrinks in X | RED: `the_clearance_envelope_encloses_the_holder` |
| the nose-centre shift has the wrong sign | RED: 5 tests |
| the edge check is off | RED: the wrong-hand test and the 180-degree bar test |
| the insert plate goes into the bands | RED: `the_insert_plate_is_left_out_of_the_bands` |

## Gate (Windows build lane, winbuild)

- Log `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-3643b-27f9f0da32829b9066b6178eb56b7bfd5d484f1a.log`, first line `head 27f9f0da32829b9066b6178eb56b7bfd5d484f1a`. The trial merge with `origin/main` (`e6849c5ae`) was a no-op.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 2 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (`tools suites: lib` ok; `app suites: turning_insert_zone` ok, because `lathe_insert_zone.rs` changed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib -- lathe_assembly tool_assembly`: 18 passed, 0 failed (the 11 spindle tests stay green after the `placed` refactor).
- The light lane did not run: only the tools lib changed. P6: no heavy step.

## Not exercised

- No caller in `crates/app` reads the lathe resolver yet. The turning laws still take their body from the current mesh path.
- Boring bar overhang in a sleeve (`projection_mm` on a bar) is not in this slice. A bar sits on the port of its sleeve.
- The approach angle is reported, but it does not change the orientation.

## Still open on #3643

- STEP, STL and OBJ mesh bodies from files (the `LatheBody::mesh` input is ready for them).
- `MCS_INSERT` as `CsysRole::Mounting` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs`.
- `crates/app/src/tool_assembly.rs` (the app side, with #3644).

Changelog: Tool assemblies: a lathe holder or boring bar with its insert resolves to the nose-centre tip, the orientation (1-8), the nose radius and one clearance body for the whole stack, with named refusals.

title: feat(pathkernel): the entry and exit stage
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

## What changed

K5 of the path kernel (#4023): the entry and exit stage, in `crates/pathkernel/src/entry/` (the record's folder: `air`, `hole`, `column`, `material`, `exit`, with `proof`, `room` and `stage`). `entry.rs` moves to `entry/proof.rs`. No old planner calls the stage. With the default planner switch, the output does not change.

- `EntryStage` tries the entries in the record's order. The asked entry outside material comes first. Then: an arc lead from the air outside the stock (#3746), a pre-drilled hole, a cleared column. A helix or a ramp into material is used only when the user selected an entry into material. A plunge is used only when asked and when the tool can plunge.
- When no entry fits, the stage refuses by name: `NO_SAFE_ENTRY` or `NO_MATERIAL_ENTRY`, at the cut start, with a fix text.
- `EntryPlanner::entry` now returns `Result<Verdict<Entry>, Refusal>`. An entry of another kind than asked carries a named `Fallback` (law 4). `named()` builds the verdict. `needs_fallback()` is the one rule.
- `Entry::led` is the single gate. It keeps the descent check of the skeleton and binds a new `Lead` (the moves in the plane onto the cut) to its room.
- The exit: `Exit::proved` checks that the lead-out starts at the end of the last cut and that the retract is at or above the material top. The lead-out goes only where the tool cuts nothing (cleared material, the band of the last cut, the air). Else the tool goes straight up. `Exit::new` now refuses an unproved lead-out.
- For Outside, the air entry keeps the tool radius from a keep-out (a clamp at the stock edge).
- `camcraft-geometry`: `geo2d::arc_points` (an arc as chords within a tolerance) and `Region::holds_path` (no stretch of a polyline outside a region), with unit tests.

## Public surface (`camcraft_pathkernel::entry`)

- `trait EntryPlanner { fn entry(..) -> Result<Verdict<Entry>, Refusal>; fn exit(..) -> Result<Exit, Refusal> }`
- `EntryStage::new(Heights, ArcChoice, chord_tol)`, `Heights::new(top, clear, retract)`, `ArcChoice::new(radius, sweep_deg)`
- `EntryChoice::with_material(MaterialChoice)`, `MaterialChoice::new(angle_deg, helix_radius)`, `DEFAULT_DESCENT_ANGLE`
- `EntryKind::name()`, `EntryKind::into_material()`, `needs_fallback(asked, used)`, `named(entry, choice, why, notes)`
- `Lead::new(pts, room)`, `Entry::led(..)`, `Entry::lead()`
- `Exit::proved(last, lead_out, retract, top)`
- Refusal reasons: `NO_SAFE_ENTRY`, `NO_MATERIAL_ENTRY`, `NOT_PLANAR`, `NO_DIRECTION`, `ENTRY_GEOMETRY`, `BAD_HEIGHTS`, `BAD_ARC`, `BAD_MATERIAL_CHOICE`, `LEAD_SHORT`, `LEAD_NOT_FLAT`, `LEAD_OFF_ROOM`, `LEAD_GAP`, `EXIT_OFF_CUT`, `RAPID_IN_MATERIAL`, `UNPROVED_LEAD_OUT`; `ROOM_TOL`
- `camcraft_geometry::geo2d::{arc_points, MAX_ARC_CHORDS}`, `Region::holds_path`

## Pins (`camcraft-pathkernel`, binary `laws`)

- `entry_stage::a_closed_pocket_with_no_hole_and_no_helix_or_ramp_is_refused_by_name` (also with a tool that can plunge: no plunge without the user's choice)
- `entry_stage::an_open_pocket_enters_in_air_with_an_arc_lead`
- `entry_stage::an_air_entry_at_the_stock_edge_keeps_off_a_clamp`
- `entry_stage::an_asked_helix_enters_the_closed_pocket_in_the_centre_area`
- `entry_stage::an_asked_helix_that_does_not_fit_falls_back_to_a_named_ramp` (and a refusal when the ramp does not fit either: never a plunge)
- `entry_stage::a_plunge_needs_the_users_choice_and_a_plunging_tool`
- `entry_stage::a_predrilled_hole_serves_the_closed_pocket`, `entry_stage::a_cleared_column_serves_the_closed_pocket`
- `exit::the_exit_leads_out_into_the_air_then_retracts`, `exit::the_exit_of_a_ring_in_uncut_material_goes_straight_up`, `exit::an_exit_is_refused_off_its_cut_or_below_the_top`
- `exit::a_lead_stays_flat_and_in_its_room_and_starts_where_the_descent_ends`, `exit::a_fallback_is_named_for_another_kind_than_asked`, `exit::the_stage_choices_refuse_bad_values_by_name`
- `l4_fallback::the_entry_stage_passes_l4_and_l5`, `l4_fallback::l4_holds_for_a_named_entry_fallback`
- A proof for another place: the existing `entry::a_descent_outside_the_proved_area_is_refused_for_each_area_proof` and `entry::a_predrilled_entry_stays_in_a_known_hole` stay green on `Entry::led`.
- `camcraft-geometry` lib: `geo2d::arc::tests::*` (4 tests).

## The law suite (#4175)

#4175 merged to the side branch before this PR. This PR changes it to the new signature:
- the stand-ins return `Ok(Verdict::done(entry))` (`standins.rs`, `l5_entry.rs`, `l4_fallback.rs`);
- `kit::Run` gets `entries: Vec<Verdict<Entry>>`; `kit::run` takes the entry out of its verdict;
- `check_l4` counts an entry as silent when `needs_fallback(asked, used)` is true and the verdict has no fallback of `Stage::Entry`. Before, it treated `ArcLead` as an entry into material.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/4178-kernel-entry-exit.md` (11 items). The main ones:
- the trait returns a `Verdict`, as the guide and the load stages do;
- the legal room of the tool centre is read from the K1 region (centre, air, the band outside each stock edge loop, less the keep-out);
- K1's air band is one tool radius wide, so the approach distance is limited to half the tool radius, with a status line note;
- one descent angle for the helix and the ramp (default 3 degrees), the helix radius at most the tool radius (default half);
- a hole narrower than the tool serves only a tool that can plunge.

## Gates (final tree)

The diff touches `camcraft-geometry`, so the quick gate falls back to batch.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/4025-kernel-region` on `0daa62a0e`: 1223 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (60.5 min, 6 jobs, under xvfb). It includes `clippy -D warnings` (all crates but kernel), `pathkernel suites: laws`, `geometry suites: lib`, and `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (all ok).
- `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/issue/4025-kernel-region`: 7 steps, 0 failed.
- K1 (#4181) merged while the gate ran. The merge of `origin/side/path-kernel` (`cc00b664f`) changes no file (`git diff HEAD^1 HEAD` is empty), so the gated tree is the tree of this head.

## Not exercised

- No kind calls the stage yet: no posted program, no CL law reading (#4154) of a kernel entry.
- The arc leads are chord points; the exact circle (G2/G3) is not recorded.
- A part that touches the stock edge (its loop is a part wall, so the band outside it is not legal room): reasoned, not pinned.
- An Inside pocket that runs off the stock enters in air only when the caller gives the outside area as `cleared`: no pin.
- `Proof` is not `#[non_exhaustive]`: a later proof kind is a breaking change of the enum. `EntryKind`, `Step` and `KernelRegion` stay open.

Effort: max
Changelog: none

Refs #4178

title: feat(tools): multi-seat indexable face mills and end mills
body:
## What changed

This PR is the `camcraft-tools` slice of #3646. It adds `milling_cutter.rs`, `milling_cutter_assembly.rs`, `milling_cutter_error.rs` and `milling_cutter_tests.rs`. There is no new crate edge, no ECS, no file I/O, and no change to `ComponentKind`.

- `MillingBody` holds the facts of a cutter body: `DC`, the cutting edge angle `KAPR`, `APMX`, `center_cutting` and an optional seat count. The seats are the body's `CSW1_1..CSW1_N` ports, or one seat port and a seat count. All seats take one shared insert.
- `derive(body, spec, insert)` gives a `MillingCutter`. `MillingCutter::tool(base)` gives the milling `Tool` record. The record has the diameter, the corner radius, `flutes = Some(seat count)`, the flute length and `center_cutting`. The running data (speed, feed, materials, cutting rows) comes from the base tool that the caller gives.
- `MillingCutter::assembled(base, nodes)` puts the cutter into a #3643 spindle assembly. It resolves the nodes itself. Three rules apply (the #4192 review):
  - **One source.** The cutter keeps the body and the insert that it was derived from. The assembly must mount exactly these two components. Another insert or another body is refused by name (`Mismatch`), also on the same diameter.
  - **Every seat.** Each seat port of the body is placed as the mounted insert is. Its cutting point must be on `DC` and in the tip plane, and its axes must be those of the mounted seat in its own radial frame. Thus each seat is the mounted seat turned about the spindle axis (`SeatOff`, with `what` = radius, height, orientation or frame). On a body with one seat port and a seat count, the other seats are copies of that port, so the check of the one port covers them.
  - **The real profile.** A body band inside the cutting depth must be inside the tool profile at the lowest point of the band. The profile includes the corner arc of a bull-nose or a round-insert cutter (`BodyOutside` gives the radius that the tool reaches there). The part above the cutting depth is enclosed over the tool (`HolderProfile::enclose`).
- The law is that the tool is never smaller than the real cutter (Prime Directive):
  - At 90 degrees the diameter is `DC`, and the corner is the nose radius of the insert. The model is exact.
  - Below 90 degrees the edge runs outward. A `DC` cylinder would be smaller than the cutter, so a gouge could pass. Thus the diameter is the reach of the edge at the top of the cutting depth: `DC + 2 * flute_len * cot(KAPR)`. This diameter is not the literal `DC` of the issue. The decision file gives the reason.
  - On a round insert the corner is half the size code (cut down to whole mm). Thus the model corner is never rounder than the insert.
  - `flute_len` is `APMX`, but no deeper than the shortest edge can rise at `KAPR`.
  - The tool's shank holds the part of the inserts above the cutting depth.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/3646-multi-seat-cutters.md`.

## Readings

- A 4-seat Ø50 90-degree face mill with `SCMT120408` gives diameter 50, corner 0.8, flutes 4 and flute length 8 (`APMX`). With `APMX` 20 the flute length is 12 (the edge).
- The same mill at 45 degrees with `APMX` 6 gives flute length 6 and diameter 62.
- A 3-seat Ø32 round-insert end mill with `RCMT1204M0` gives corner 6 and flute length 4.
- In a BT40 assembly the gauge length is 95. The tool holds the holder (holder Ø50) and the cutter body.
- Ø50, 90 degrees, `SCMT120408`: a body down to the tip at r 24.8 is refused; the tool reaches r 24.2 at the tip. A body at r 24.2 passes.
- Ø32 round insert `RCMT1204M0`: a body down to the tip at r 15 is refused; the tool reaches r 10 at the tip. A body at r 9.5 passes.

## Pinning tests (`camcraft-tools` lib, `milling_cutter_tests`)

- `a_face_mill_and_an_end_mill_share_one_insert`: a face mill and a shoulder end mill share one insert. An edit of the insert changes the corner on the two mills.
- `a_45_degree_face_mill_cuts_its_edge_reach`
- `a_round_insert_end_mill_takes_half_its_insert_as_corner`
- `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter`: the envelope pin. It samples the real meridian outline: the edges, the nose arc, the full insert at 90, 75, 45 and 20 degrees, and a round insert of its metric size and its inch size.
- `the_assembled_face_mill_encloses_holder_and_body`: the gauge length and the enclosed body. A body outside the cutter inside the cutting depth is refused, and so are seats off `DC`.
- `a_body_outside_the_rounded_corner_is_refused` (review finding 1): a bull-nose and a round-insert cutter, each with a body that is refused and a body that passes.
- `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` (review finding 2): the selected seat `CSW1_1` is valid. A second seat on Ø80, a third seat 1 mm off the tip plane and a fourth seat turned 10 degrees are each refused by port. A one-port body with a seat count of 4 passes.
- `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused` (review finding 3): the shared insert changes to `SCMT120400` before the assembly, and another cutter body. Both are refused.
- The three new pins are the reviewer probes in the new API. The probes in the old API (`assembled(base, resolved)`) failed on `25eca3ba4` on winbuild: 4 of 4 red (bull-nose body, round body, second seat on Ø80, changed insert).
- `seats_that_do_not_take_the_insert_are_refused_by_the_fit_checks`: the #3642 `FitError` (size, shape, kind).
- `degenerate_cutters_are_refused_by_name`: NaN and infinite values, `DC` <= 0, `APMX` 0, a bad `KAPR`, 0 seats, a seat count that does not agree with the ports, 33 seats, a body that is not a tool item, and corners that do not fit.

## The mutation

m1 to m4 ran on winbuild against head `25eca3ba4`. m5 to m10 ran on winbuild against the fix files (`milling_cutter_assembly.rs`). Each one made a pin red, and the clone was restored after each one.

| Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|
| m1: below 90 degrees the diameter is `DC` (the literal of the issue) | `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter`, `a_45_degree_face_mill_cuts_its_edge_reach`, `the_assembled_face_mill_encloses_holder_and_body` |
| m2: the shank does not hold the inserts (`shank_d = diameter`) | `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter` |
| m3: the round corner is the size code plus 1 mm (rounder than the insert) | `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter`, `a_round_insert_end_mill_takes_half_its_insert_as_corner` |
| m4: a body outside the cutter inside the cutting depth passes | `the_assembled_face_mill_encloses_holder_and_body` |
| m5: the body check uses `diameter / 2`, not the profile (finding 1) | `a_body_outside_the_rounded_corner_is_refused` |
| m6: no radius check on the other seats (finding 2) | `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` |
| m7: no height check on the other seats (finding 2) | `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` |
| m8: no orientation check on the other seats (finding 2) | `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one` |
| m9: no check of the mounted insert against the derived one (finding 3) | `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused` |
| m10: no check of the mounted body against the derived one (finding 3) | `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused` |

## The Windows gate (winbuild)

- Head `1366f4942ea925b12b839aabf109388f1de330df` (the first line of `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-4192-1366f4942.log`), trial-merged with `origin/main` `72890060b` (clean).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the plan has 1 step, `tools suites: lib`. Result: ok, 186 passed, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The light lane did not run, because no code outside the tools lib changed. This PR is P6, so it gets no heavy step.

## Not exercised

- No app code changed. `crates/app` and the UI do not read the new module yet.
- No operation ran with a derived tool (the plunge refusal and the collision checks on an operation). These need the document record of #3644.

## What is left on #3646

- The app part (`crates/app/src/tool_assembly.rs`): the document record, the edit of a shared insert that marks the milling operations `Stale`, and the plunge refusal and collision tests on an indexable face mill. This part waits for #3644, which is in work now.
- `tool_material` and cutting rows that come from the insert. The #3642 insert component does not carry them yet.

Changelog: none (domain code only; the user sees it when #3644 stores the cutter)

Effort: high

title: fix(finish3d): start and exit picks for 3D Finish
body:
Slice 2 of #3329: the 3D Finish takes a start point and an exit point on its Parallel pattern. Deburr is slice 1 (#4168). The 3D Pocket stays open.

## Behaviour

- `OpType::Finish3D` has the capability `PickCapability::Raster`, as the Face and the 5-Axis Parallel.
- On the Parallel pattern, at any pass direction, a pick chooses a corner of the zigzag raster. The order law is the raster seam of #3330 (`finishing3d::raster_seam::order`):
  - Start: the corner nearest the start pick. The pass order is reversed, or each pass runs the other way.
  - Exit: the order whose last pass ends nearest the exit pick.
- The cut geometry does not change. Only the order and the direction of the passes change. The links are planned again on the new order by the raster's own link laws.
- New motion entry `finishing3d::finish_seamed` (the angled Parallel raster with the picks) and the check `finishing3d::raster_ends_kept`.
- No pick: the arm calls the same generator as before. The path is byte-identical.
- MCP: `edit_operation` sets the picks (the existing `picks` field). Its schema names "3D Finish (the Parallel pattern only; ...)". Undo and redo go through `EditOperationParams`.

## Refusals (by name, never moved)

1. A pick on any pattern but Parallel. Refused at the command door (`pick_refusal`) and again in the generator.
2. A pick farther than 1.5 tool diameters from every corner, and an exit that the start's order cannot end at (the shared raster seam).
3. A pick on a model with no shallow ground.
4. A plunge column at the picked start, or a retract column at the picked exit, within the ball radius of the part. Exact: `support::column_clear` (segment-to-facet distance), no sampling.
5. One rule for a moved corner (`raster_ends_kept`): the finished path is read again. Its first cut must land on the picked start corner, and its last feed must end on the picked exit corner. This closes the class "a later stage moves a picked corner". Today it catches:
   - an exit when the waterline rings cut after the raster (motion);
   - a corner that the area controls clip away (application, after the clip and the centre-cutting guard).

## Mutations

Each mutation was applied alone on head b377b0561 and then restored. Each turned the named tests red:

| # | Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | motion: skip `raster_ends_kept` after the rings | `multiaxis finish_seam::finish_with_waterlines_keeps_a_start_and_refuses_an_exit_by_name` |
| M2 | app: skip the post-clip `raster_ends_kept` | `start_exit_shared finish3d::finish3d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` |
| M3 | motion: `ends_clear` always `Ok` | both `finish_seam_tests` (2 of 2) |
| M4 | app: remove the door refusal of another pattern | `finish3d::finish3d_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_another_pattern_is_refused_at_the_door` |
| M5 | motion: remove the generator's pattern refusal | `finish_seam::finish_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` |
| M6 | app: the arm ignores the picks | `finish3d_starts_at_the_picked_corner...` and `finish3d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` |
| M7 | motion: `raster_ends_kept` compares the exit with the start tip | 3 of 5 `finish_seam` tests |

## Readings

- With 90 and 30 degree passes on the floor-and-block fixture: a start at the automatic end and an exit at the automatic start both reverse the whole raster. The first cut lands exactly on the picked corner and the last feed ends exactly on the other corner (to 1e-9). The tool rises straight up.
- Picks at the automatic corners give the automatic path, move for move.
- Each move of each picked path keeps more than `R - 0.05` mm from every facet (exact segment-to-facet distance). Both moved columns keep the full radius.
- Through `generate` on the 30 x 20 x 10 block (angle 90): a start at the far end of the first pass plunges at `(a.x, -a.y)`. An exit at the automatic start ends the cut there.
- The same exit with the waterline rings on is refused ("the waterline rings cut after the raster"). An area offset of -6 mm with a start pick is refused ("the area controls clip the raster").
- Both picks at one corner are refused by name. No exit is moved. This is the same rule that the Deburr fix (#4168) uses, written down in the decision file.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion --lib finishing3d::finish_seam_tests` (2): the exact column law, with a canopy, at the ball radius (3.000 passes, 2.999 is refused).
- `camcraft-motion --test multiaxis finish_seam` (5): byte-identical without a pick at three angles; start, exit and both picks at 90 and 30 degrees (each cut sampled every 0.25 mm on the automatic raster and back; every move's ball segment checked exactly against each facet; both moved columns checked exactly); the waterline exit refusal; each pattern refusal; the moved-corner rule.
- `camcraft-app --test start_exit_shared finish3d` (3): the started and exited raster through `generate` (far end of the first pass, the whole raster reversed, straight rise, top cuts sampled every 0.25 mm), the refusals (far pick, rings, area controls), MCP edit, the door refusal of another pattern, undo and redo, the schema text.
- `start_exit_shared::every_kind_has_one_pick_capability...` now expects `Raster` for the 3D Finish.

## Goldens moved

None. No fixture, golden, recorded program or snapshot changed.

## Not exercised

- Picks on the other 3D Finish patterns: refused by name (see the decision file for why).
- The UI has no 3D Finish start / exit rows yet, as for the 5-axis slices. The picks are set through MCP and the project file.
- The full heavy lanes (P2: no heavy step).

## Remaining kinds of #3329

3D Pocket.

## Gate

Mac lane (the Mac gate lock), head `61d5b61ed`. The first line of each log is that head.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 217 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 32.3 min. The plan holds `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl`, `start_exit_shared`, motion `lib` and `multiaxis`. All ok.
  - Three earlier attempts on this head stopped at the first build step, before any test ran. The error was E0463 "can't find crate". The dependency metadata in this worktree's debug target was unreadable after the target folder changed outside this run (also without sccache). I deleted the worktree's `target/debug` and the fourth run passed. No code changed between the runs.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- No heavy step (P2).

Decision: `docs/decisions/3329-finish3d-picks.md`.

Changelog: 3D Finish: a start point and an exit point choose the corner of the Parallel raster where the cut starts and where its last pass ends; a pick that the raster cannot keep is refused by name.

Effort: max

title: fix(mcp): configure the live client idle timeout
body:
## What changed

The live MCP app accepts `--mcp-idle-timeout <seconds>` and
`CAMCRAFT_MCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT`. The option wins over the environment value.
The default stays 300 seconds. Zero disables idle expiry.

The app uses the configured window for its TCP listener and authenticated
UI link clients. The UI link still requires a valid hello within five
seconds. Framing limits, shutdown polling and one-client ownership stay
unchanged. The stdio bridge does not reconnect automatically.

Invalid values produce a named startup error. Seconds must be non-negative
whole numbers that fit `u64`. The help text, start guide and MCP skill
describe the option.

## Verification

Behavioral red tests on current main proved that zero was clamped to the
poll step and that the UI rejected the new option. Both now pass.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live -- --test-threads=3`
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib cli_options_tests -- --test-threads=3`
- Selected quick gate (pass: `mcp_live` 29 tests; UI library 1714 passed, 8 ignored): `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --only 'app suites: mcp_live' --only 'ui suites: lib'`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test mcp_live -- -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --lib -- -D warnings`: pass.
- Site tests `test_ai_guide.py` and `test_guide_after_1995.py`: 10 pass.
- `git diff --check`: pass.

The tests cover defaults, CLI and environment precedence, zero, invalid and
overflow values, finite expiry, prompt shutdown and the pre-hello deadline.
All socket tests use synthetic local connections.

The full quick plan selects 179 steps because the MCP re-export maps to
167 app suites. Only the transport and UI-library steps run here.
`cargo xtask gate light --dry-run` requires a release build of app and
motion plus unrelated geometry tests. The light lane was not run. A dry run
is not a pass. No post, toolpath, geometry or simulation code changes.
No catalog, full-workspace, release, physical-machine or Windows check ran.

## Before and after CLI help

Both images show actual `target/debug/camcraft-ui --help` output. Each command exited with code 0.
I built each unmodified revision on Linux with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo build -j 3 -p camcraft-ui --bin camcraft-ui`.
The browser displays the captured stderr. Only ANSI color codes were removed. No help text was edited.

**Before:** parent revision `e6849c5aea183b81135c8143955cc8c88a429a89`.

title: feat(pathkernel): the ring and row guide planners
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Sub-PR 1 of 2 for #4176 (K2, the guide stage). This PR adds the ring and the row guide planners: the two families that 2D Pocket needs. Part 2 (the medial line, the trace of a chain and the helix) follows on the same issue.

## What changed

Public surface in `camcraft_pathkernel::guide`:
- `RingPlanner`: rings as level sets of the distance to the walls (Held 1991), spaced by the stepover of the choice. `RingRef::Boundary` uses all edges. `RingRef::Part` uses the part walls only; its rings are open at the stock edge.
- Clean-up rings fill the area that the regular rings leave. The 0.1 mm2 guard makes the result `Incomplete` with each gap named.
- `RowPlanner`: rows at the angle, spaced evenly at the stepover or less, clipped to the cutter-centre area. A closing ring is added on request.
- `Guides`: sends rings and rows to their planners. It refuses the medial line and the trace with `FAMILY_NOT_YET` until part 2 (law 4).
- `Mark`, `MarkKind` (`FullWidth`, `Fill`, `Closing`; `#[non_exhaustive]`), `Span`. `GuideSet::with_marks` and `GuideSet::marks`. `GuideSet::new` does not change.
- `FullWidth` names each stretch where the tool disc overlaps no disc of the next deeper curves and no air (#3788). K3 and K4 read it.
- Named refusals: `NOT_RINGS`, `NOT_ROWS`, `CIRCLE_NOT_YET`, `BAND_NOT_YET`, `OFFSET_BELOW_CENTER`, `WALL_STRIP_UNCUT`, `NO_RING`, `TOO_MANY_RINGS`, `TOO_MANY_ROWS`, `STEP_ABOVE_DIAMETER`, `BAD_TOL`, `NOT_PLANAR`, `GUIDE_GEOMETRY`, `BAD_STRETCH`, `MARK_NO_CURVE`, `MARK_OFF_CURVE`.

The kernel crate still depends on `camcraft-geometry` only. No geometry function was added. No old planner and no golden changes: with the default switch the output is identical.

## Pins

- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/guide_rings.rs` (11 tests): level-set spacing, law 1 under a permuted selection, Part equal to Boundary without a stock edge, the waist (two lobes, a neck narrower than two steps: the full-width stretch of each strand is named), clean-up rings, a small piece kept (0.01 mm2), a ring count, rings round a part, each refusal, `Guides`.
- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/guide_rows.rs` (6 tests): row spacing, rows at an angle with a closing ring, gaps named without a closing ring, law 1, refusals, mark checks. Helpers in `guide_kit.rs`.
- `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_levels/kernel_rings.rs`: the kernel rings against the recorded old rings (#3750 goldens). Readings (agreement within 0.02 mm):
  - Dog bone, 2D Offset round the part: each point of the 29 kernel rings is on each of the 7 old plans with a known stock. Named difference: the old plan also walks the stock outline; the kernel does not, because the outline is air (#4025 decision 4).
  - `auto_blind` is not compared: an Outside kernel region needs the stock.
  - The band round the disc: the 2D Pocket rings and the 3-D level rings are the old Auto rings, both ways. Named difference: the old Inside and Outside plans build their own pieces for each start side (#3316, #3750).
- Law suite registry: this PR adds no registry row. When 2D Pocket moves, its row in `tests/laws/registry.rs` becomes `State::Moved` with `Planners { guide: Box::new(Guides), .. }`.

## Gates on the final head `74766eaa5` (base `origin/side/path-kernel`)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: green (pathkernel lib, pathkernel laws, motion pass_start_levels).
- The whole pathkernel `laws` suite: 98 passed (the guard grids included).
- Motion `kernel_rings` and `kernel_baseline` pins: 17 passed.
- `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: green.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: green, 7 of 7 steps.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Review fixes (review of head 8977cd5f0)

- Finding 1 (the guard area was narrowed by the first offset): commit f54a11059. One guard for both planners reads the whole centre area. `WALL_STRIP_UNCUT` refuses a clearing ring choice with a first offset above the tool radius. A ring count names the uncut area in a note.
- Findings 2 to 4 (a dropped mark, the closing ring round an island, a full-width stretch on an open ring): commit 74766eaa5.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/4176-kernel-guides-rings-rows.md`.

## Not exercised

- No planner calls the new code yet (no recipe on the kernel). The fig8 outline is not compared in this PR.
- Exact circle rings and the band reference are refused by name: they come with the helix guide (part 2) and K4.

title: fix(app): a "parameters are not usable" refusal names the field and its rule
body:
## What changed

`add_operation` and `edit_operation` (and the commands behind them, `CreateOperation`, `EditOperationParams` and `ChangeOperationKind`) refused a bad number with a sentence that does not name the field:

> operation parameters are not usable for a 2D Pocket operation

An agent or a script user could not tell what to correct. Found in the local-model MCP benchmark of 2026-11-22.

When `OpParams::is_sane` fails, a new helper, `commands/operation/field_refusal.rs`, reads the parameters through `project::params_to_json` (the field names that MCP and the project file use) and adds the first shared field that breaks its rule:

- `stepdown`, `stepover`, `feed`, `plunge_feed`, `tolerance`, `helix_radius`: greater than 0
- `stock_to_leave`: 0 or more

Now:

> operation parameters are not usable for a 2D Pocket operation: stepdown must be greater than 0 (got -3)

Notes for the review:

- Only top-level fields are read. Every kind that has one of these fields at the top level asks the same rule of it (checked against each arm of `is_sane` and the plasma, waterjet, wire, sinker and undercut doors). A nested block with its own rules, such as the wire's 4-axis `tolerance` (0..=10), is not read.
- The helper runs only after `is_sane` has failed, so it can only name a field that really breaks its rule. If the cause is something else (a height, an angle, a kind-specific field), the refusal is the old sentence, unchanged.
- The start of the sentence does not change, so tests and agents that match on "operation parameters are not usable" still match.
- The project load check (`project/validate.rs`) is not changed.

## How tested

- New test `mcp_pockets::a_bad_pocket_parameter_is_refused_by_field_name`: `stepdown: -3` and `stock_to_leave: -0.5` through `edit_operation` (the operation is unchanged after the refusal), and `feed: 0` through `add_operation` (no operation is created).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base main`: 24 of 27 steps pass on the first run. The 3 red steps (`lib` `lathe_voice::tests::the_door_refuses_on_every_turning_dialect_and_passes_every_milling_one`, `sinker_burn`, `wire_tool`) failed with "cannot find the file" for the Sodick post and machine files: my `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` was inside another, older checkout, and the data folders resolve by walking up from the test exe. All three pass with a target dir outside any checkout.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test mcp_pockets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- By hand over MCP (`camcraft-cli mcp`), the same `edit_operation` call on `main` and on this branch gives the two sentences above.

Changelog: An operation refused for a bad number now names the field and its rule, for example "stepdown must be greater than 0 (got -3)".

title: fix(post): Haas NGC safe start, end retract, M4 and coolant-off codes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/haas.cps` now writes these NGC words. The source is the Haas Mill NGC Operator's Manual, 2025 edition (public on haascnc.com). The page numbers are the printed page numbers.

| #1977 item | State | Change and source |
|---|---|---|
| `G91` modal at `M30` | fixed | `retractHome()` writes `G90` directly after each `G91 G28` retract: the program end, a setup-change stop, and a trip home. The end is now `G91 G28 Z0` / `G28 X0 Y0` / `G90` / `M30`. Sample program, p. 449; G28, p. 337. |
| `G53` retract | fixed | `G53 G49 G0 Z<safeRetractZ>`. A home ask (the program end, a trip home) adds `G53 G0 Y0.`. A setup-change stop lifts Z only. "Completion" blocks, pp. 202 and 204. The next section's tool call writes `G43 H<n>` again. |
| Retract choice documented | fixed | `docs/decisions/1977-haas-ngc-words.md`. The default stays `G28` (now with `G90`). `G53` stays an option. |
| `G94` in the safe-start block | fixed | `G17 G90 G94 G5x G40 G49 G80`. G94, p. 386. |
| `M4` reverse spindle | fixed | `millSpindleReverse = true`. `PARAM MillSpindle reverse` starts `S.. M4`. The next section starts `M3` again. M03/M04, p. 436. `Haas` is removed from `tool_gate.rs::M3_ONLY_POSTS`, as decision 4031 says. A G84 under M4 is refused by name (G84 is the right-hand tap: pp. 224, 381). |
| `explains = "paren"` + `explain(words)` | already fixed | PR #1814 (#1388), on main. This PR adds `explainWords` for the Haas meaning of G76 (fine bore, p. 371) and of M7, M73/M74, M83/M84, M88/M89. |
| Coolant-off codes | fixed | M88 -> M89 (p. 449), M83 -> M84 (p. 449), M73 -> M74 (p. 447). M9 stays for M8 and M7 (the NGC shower coolant: M09 stops it, p. 438), and for any other start code. |
| `G74` left-hand tapping | left | The app refuses a left-hand tap before the post runs (`posting_family.rs`, #1453). The stream has no word for the tap hand. G74 needs a stream word, a manifest flag and app changes. The refusal is safe in the meantime. This item stays open on #1977. |

Also left: the manual says to write `M88` before the spindle speed (p. 449). The post writes it after `S.. M3`. The control then stops and starts the spindle again. This is slower, not unsafe. It stays open on #1977 too.

## Pinning tests (each fails on `origin/main`'s `haas.cps`)

- `crates/post/tests/setup_change.rs`: `haas_safe_start_block_states_feed_per_minute`, `haas_program_end_restores_absolute_mode_before_m30`, `haas_g53_retract_cancels_the_length_offset_and_brings_y_home`
- `crates/post/tests/haas_dwell_cycles.rs`: `haas_reverse_mill_spindle_starts_m4_for_its_section_only`, `haas_refuses_a_right_hand_tap_under_a_reverse_spindle`
- `crates/app/tests/coolant_followups.rs`: `haas_stops_each_coolant_option_with_its_own_off_code`
- `crates/app/tests/thread_passes.rs`: `a_left_hand_cut_mill_under_m4_climbs_clockwise_and_posts_m4` (Haas now posts M4. The refusal side uses `tormach.cps`.)
- `crates/app/tests/cutter_hand.rs`: Haas leaves `M3_ONLY`. The M3-only check in `an_edit_to_left_hand_refuses_generation_and_post_until_the_operation_asks` uses Tormach PathPilot.

## Goldens moved

33 Haas goldens changed:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/haas/*.nc` (17)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/haas/*.nc` (2)
- `inverted/haas_x.nc`, `program_entry/haas_pause_home.nc`, `synth_haas.nc`
- `crates/post/tests/golden/{bore,explain,fine_bore,ream}/haas.nc`
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/haas/*.nc` (7)

Each golden has the same two edits, and nothing else changed:

1. The safe-start line gets `G94` after `G90` (in each section).
2. After the program-end `G28 X0 Y0`, a new line `G90` comes before `M30`. In `program_entry/haas_pause_home.nc`, the `G90` was already there (a trip home), so only `G94` changed.

The explain golden also reads `(XY PLANE, ABSOLUTE POSITIONS, FEED PER MINUTE)` on the safe-start line. "WORK OFFSET 1" no longer fits the 60-character comment budget, so the explain helper drops it. The new `G90` line reads `(ABSOLUTE POSITIONS)`.

The `macro_b` reader of `inverted_probe.rs` now accepts `G94` as a no-op, because it is the only feed mode that the reader reads.

## Readings

On `origin/main`, the default program end is `G91 G28 Z0` / `G28 X0 Y0` / `M30`, and `G91` is active at `M30`. On this branch it is `G91 G28 Z0` / `G28 X0 Y0` / `G90` / `M30`. In G53 mode it is `G53 G49 G0 Z0.` / `G53 G0 Y0.` / `M30` on the shipped Haas machines (`safeRetractZ` 0).

- M73/M74 and M83/M84 were not tested on a machine that has the Tool Air Blast or Auto Air Gun option. The shipped Haas machine files state only `Flood M8`.
