title: fix(contour): Do not touch for 2D Contour operations
body:
## What changed

- 2D Contour takes "Do not touch" protected faces and edges (`do_not_touch_applies`). The Boundary group of a Contour shows "Pick protected", and a viewport click adds a face row or an edge row.
- Each Contour mode has an avoid-aware twin in `camcraft-motion` (`contour_avoid*` modules):
  - closed rings, rings on a part, picked rings;
  - the whole-model contour;
  - open chains, open runs on the part side and on the stock side;
  - DXF sketch loops and chains (`contour_sketch.rs`).
- Each twin keeps the flutes, the shank and the holder clear of each protected item, by the clearance. This applies to cuts, leads, links and plunges.
- A ring is clipped at each level against the keep-out of the full tool. The kept pieces are cut as open pieces. A lead, a link or an entry that enters the keep-out is dropped or moved.
- A ring or a chain that is blocked on every level is skipped. A note names the protected items. When no cut remains, the operation is refused, and the refusal names the items. Control compensation that a clip would break is refused by name.
- Each result goes through the full-tool verify before it leaves the generator. The app verify and the post gate read the Contour moves as they read the other kinds (`verify_avoid`).
- With no protected item, each twin calls the plain generator. The toolpath does not change.
- The MCP tool text and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` list 2D Contour.

This PR resumes the held branch of 2026-11-22 (1993c0cf1). That work was never built. The merge of main needed these changes:

- Ports into the avoid emitter of what main changed in `contour::emit_band`: the ring entry (#3830, #3917), the pecked dive (#3678), the picked seam under compensation (#1473), the tab level start (#3453), the picked ladder, and the start/exit picks that moved to `ContourParams::picks`.
- Two real defects in the held code, found by the pins:
  - A clipped piece ended on the keep-out boundary. `Region::contains` counts the boundary as inside. Each piece without a lead read as blocked and was dropped, so a bore with a protected pin cut nothing. Fix: the piece ends step 0.001 mm back (`END_TRIM`).
  - A bore-side piece entry fell back to the whole centre region, without the keep-out. The entry dived beside the protected pin, and the shank came 0.83 mm short of the clearance. The final verify refused it, so no G-code was wrong. Fix: the entry room is always the centre less the keep-out; an entry point outside it grazes at itself.

## Cause

`do_not_touch_applies` did not list `OpType::Contour`, and the Contour generators had no keep-out law.

## Tests

Pins (all red before the change, green after):

- `camcraft-motion --test avoid_contour`:
  - `empty_avoid_matches_plain_contour_paths_exactly`
  - `contour_avoid_closed_partial_tabs_inside_whole_and_open_stay_clear`
  - `contour_avoid_refuses_unavoidable_control_and_blocked_pick_by_name`
- `camcraft-app --test do_not_touch` (new submodule `do_not_touch/contour.rs`):
  - `contour::contour_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge` (no posted move nearer than the clearance, checked on the NC)
  - `contour::contour_do_not_touch_refuses_unavoidable_cut_and_blocks_post` (refusal names the item; post blocked; no NC file)
  - `contour::contour_without_do_not_touch_keeps_same_toolpath` (same NC with and without an empty protection)
  - `contour::contour_modes_picked_open_and_dxf_sketch_stay_clear`
- `camcraft-ui --lib`:
  - `egui_app::tests::do_not_touch::contour_shows_pick_protected_and_no_unsupported_note`
  - `egui_app::tests::do_not_touch_click::contour_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click`

Mutation checks (each guard put back to the old code, pins run, then restored):

- M1 `do_not_touch_applies` without Contour: 3 app pins red, 2 UI pins red. The baseline pin stays green.
- M2 no `END_TRIM` step: `contour_avoid_closed_partial_...` red ("no safe cutting room remains").
- M3 bore entry falls back to the whole centre: `contour_avoid_closed_partial_...` red (shank 0.829 mm short).
- M4 the Contour dispatch in `generate.rs` ignores protection: 3 app pins red (gouges, missing refusal). The baseline pin stays green.

Expected-change tests:

- `pocket3d_do_not_touch_keeps_clear_raises_links_and_blocks_impossible_cut` used a Contour as its unsupported kind. It uses a Slot now, and the message check also reads "2D Contour".
- The UI test `unsupported_op_shows_do_not_touch_note_without_pick_button` used a Contour. Each kind that has a Boundary group now takes protection, so no kind shows that note in the UI. The test is now `contour_shows_pick_protected_and_no_unsupported_note`. The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by one.

Fixture changes in the new pins, with the reason:

- The shared fixture's stock is 24 mm tall, and the pins cut the plate at Z 10..5. Main's flute law (#3525) blocks a 15 mm flute there, with or without protection. The pins edit the tool to a 25 mm flute and a 2 mm shank. The holder base stays at tip + 27 mm.
- The NC check measures the true 3D gap of each tool band to the protected box.
- The plain tilted (3+2) Contour and the plain sketch Contour of the fixture already have gouge and crossing findings on main. For those two cases the pins check only what protection adds: no `avoid_hit`, and (sketch) no finding kind that the plain path lacks.

Commands on the final head (c50a967e8):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 339 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (37.8 min). It includes `ui suites: lib`, where the two UI pins ran and passed on this box.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The quick gate ran `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and `golden_cl`: green.
- Heavy lanes: not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 111 steps (the app and motion heavy lanes). AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) gives a P3 PR no heavy step; the light lane is the review's step.

## Goldens moved

None. The diff changes no `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file, and the catalog and golden suites above are green.

## Not exercised

- The tilted (3+2) Contour with protection gets a `rapid_in_part` finding that the plain tilted path does not have. The plain tilted path already has gouge findings in this fixture, so the post is blocked in both cases. Follow-up: #4131.
- No "incomplete" operation status exists. A blocked ring or chain is skipped with a named note, as Bore and the Pocket and Trace protection do. See `docs/decisions/3344-contour-do-not-touch.md`.
- No UI screenshots: the change shows an existing button for one more kind. The UI pins assert the button and the viewport clicks.

## Overlaps

Open PRs that touch the same files, different functions or rows; whichever merges second refreshes:

- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: #4050, #4028, #4008, #3832, #3103 (other operation arms; this PR changes the Contour arm only).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`: #4028, #4008, #3103 (module and `pub use` lists).
- `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`: #4050, #3963 (other tool rows).

New top-level test file: `crates/motion/tests/avoid_contour.rs`. Reason: `crates/motion/tests/` has no directory suite for the avoid laws; its siblings `avoid_pocket.rs`, `avoid_adaptive.rs` and `avoid_engrave.rs` are top-level files too. The app pins joined the `do_not_touch` directory suite.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Process change: yes

Changelog: 2D Contour takes "Do not touch" faces and edges: the full tool stays clear of them on cuts, leads, links and plunges, and a cut that cannot keep clear is refused by name.

Fixes #3344

title: feat(pathkernel): the crate skeleton, the stage types and the planner switch
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

## What this PR adds

- The new crate `camcraft-pathkernel` in `crates/pathkernel/`. It depends only on `camcraft-geometry`. `camcraft-motion` depends on it and re-exports it as `camcraft_motion::pathkernel`. The app gets it through that re-export (`camcraft_app::pathkernel`). There is no direct app edge.
- The stage types of the record, with no planner logic. **One rule for the crate: valid by construction.** A value of a public type is always valid. A field that could hold an invalid value is private and is set only by a checked constructor. An enum variant with data holds a validated newtype. A list holds only validated records, and its constructor checks the rules between them (decision 12).
  - `verdict`: `Stage`, `Refusal` (a blank reason becomes `NO_REASON`), `Fallback`, `Gap`, `Gaps` (one or more), `Note`, `Verdict<T>`.
  - `frame`: `Spot`, `Positive`, `WorkPlane::Planar(PlanarFrame)`, `AxisControl::Normal`, `ToolShape::Disc(Disc)`, `PlanePoint`.
  - `region`: `MaterialSide`, `Bounds`, `KernelRegion::Planar(PlanarRegion)`.
  - `guide`: `RingRef`, `Circle`, `GuideChoice` (`Rings(RingsChoice)`, `Rows(RowsChoice)`, `Medial`, `Trace(TraceOffset)`), `Family`, `Curve` (with `same_cut`), `GuideSet` (a total order), trait `GuidePlanner`.
  - `order`: `StartSide`, `Direction`, `OrderChoice`, `OrderedSet` (law 3: only a permutation, a restart and a reversal), trait `OrderPlanner`.
  - `load`: `PLAN_TOL`, `Engagement`, `Trochoid`, `ConstantLoad`, `LoadControl`, `Reach`, `Reading`, `OverLimit`, `Controlled` (law 6), traits `StockRead` and `LoadPlanner`.
  - `link`: `LinkPolicy`, `Hop` (`Stay(StayPath)`, `Lift(LiftReason)`), `LinkTally`, trait `LinkProof`.
  - `entry`: `EntryKind`, `Area`, `Hole`, `EntryChoice`, `Proof` (each proof names its place), `Entry` (approach and descent; law 5), `Exit`, trait `EntryPlanner`.
  - `plan`: `Cut`, `Step` (`#[non_exhaustive]`), `Plan` (the step law as a transition table).
  - `recipe`: `Recipe`. `engine`: `PLANNER_ENV`, `PlannerEngine` (default `Old`), `engine_from_switch`.
- The one switch: `crates/app/src/operation/planner_switch.rs`.
  - `planner_engine()` reads `CAMCRAFT_PLANNER` one time for each process. No other code reads the setting.
  - `check_engine(kind, engine)` runs in `run_job` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs`), before every arm of `run_job_arms`. The arms do not change.
  - The default is the old planner. With `new`, each of the 16 phase-1 kinds is refused by name ("the new path planner does not plan <kind> yet"). There is no fallback and no panic. A bad value gives the old planner and one diagnostic.
- The xtask entries:
  - The crate is in `ALL_CRATES`, `BATCH_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` (`xtask/src/plan.rs`). It is not in `SHARED` and not in `HEAVY_CRATES` (record). The heavy reach to motion and app comes from the manifests.
  - The hand-pinned tests are updated: `heavy_plan_tests.rs` (reach), `select_tests.rs`, `tests.rs`, `step_tests.rs`.
  - A new test checks the gate lists against the workspace members.
  - AGENTS.md "Check only the touched crates" names `camcraft-pathkernel`.
- The #3750 baseline goldens and their pins are cherry-picked from `9c69f004a` (`origin/issue/3750-shared-ring-set`). The pick applies cleanly.

## Dependency decision

The record `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md`, section "Dependency decision", is the decision for the two new edges. The choices of this step are in `docs/decisions/4055-pathkernel-skeleton.md` (items 1 to 17; items 12 to 17 are the rules of the review rework).

## Goldens moved

These 17 files are additions. They are copied unchanged from commit `9c69f004a` (`origin/issue/3750-shared-ring-set`), recorded on `origin/main` `138a592a1`. This PR changes no recorded program.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/offset2d_fig8_auto.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/offset2d_fig8_inside.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/offset2d_fig8_inside_arc.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/offset2d_fig8_outside.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/offset2d_fig8_outside_arc.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/level_rings_band.txt`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_auto.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_auto_blind.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_inside.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_inside_arc.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_inside_rings.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_outside.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_outside_arc.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/offset2d_dogbone_outside_rings.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/pocket_band_auto.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/pocket_band_inside.cl`
- `crates/motion/tests/golden/pocket_band_outside.cl`

## Pins

- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws.rs`, a new directory suite with one submodule for each stage. The tests use the public API only. New top-level test file: the new crate has no suite yet, and the record puts the K7 law suite (#4027) in this directory. The tests:
  - `construction`: each constructor refuses NaN, infinity, zero, an empty list and a blank reason by name (finding 3).
  - `order`: restarts and reversals pass; the crossing square, a swapped vertex order, a shifted open curve, a changed circle, a changed index, a changed family and a moved point are refused (finding 1).
  - `plan`: each cell of the transition table, with two disconnected cuts in a row (finding 2).
  - `entry`: a descent outside the proved place is refused for each proof kind, and a hole proof for another hole is refused (finding 4).
  - `load`: the limit domain, malformed records, double, stray and mismatched records (finding 5).
  - `guide`: all 24 input orders of four curves with equal keys give one set; equal lowest points give one start (finding 6).
- The unit tests of `engine` (3).
- `switch_default_is_the_old_planner` (app, `offset_pass_start`, heavy lane): the 2D Offset Inside on `fig8.step`, through the dispatch with the switch at its default, against the #3750 golden `offset2d_fig8_inside.cl`.
- `switch_default_passes_each_phase1_kind_to_the_old_planner` and `switch_new_refuses_a_kind_it_does_not_plan_yet` (app, `offset_pass_start`, default suite).
- The #3750 baseline pins (cherry-picked): `offset2d_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner`, `pocket_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner` and `level_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner` (motion, `pass_start_levels`), and `fig8_offset_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner` (app, heavy).
- cl: `cl_text_round_trips_every_golden` (it now accepts the annotation tail of a golden).
- xtask: `the_gate_lists_name_every_workspace_crate`, `a_pathkernel_change_plans_its_suites_and_the_mapped_app_suite`, `reach_follows_the_crate_dependencies`.

## Gate results

All results are on the final head `9ea79086c`. The base `origin/side/path-kernel` is `d1feeb12d`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` under `xvfb-run -a`: the gate makes it a batch, because `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` change. 1222 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (60.1 min). This includes:
  - `pathkernel suites: lib` and `pathkernel suites: laws`;
  - `app suites: offset_pass_start`;
  - `motion suites: pass_start_levels` (the #3750 baseline pins for 2D Offset, 2D Pocket and the level rings);
  - `cl suites: headless_bin`;
  - clippy `-D warnings` on the `CLIPPY` list (pathkernel, motion and app included).

title: fix(post): refuse a left-hand cutter on posts that cannot reverse the spindle
body:
fix(post): refuse a left-hand cutter on posts that cannot reverse the spindle

#4031, steps 1, 2 and 5 (the maintainer scoped the work; steps 3 and 4
are the follow-up #4102).

What changed:
- `Tool` gains `cutter_hand` (`crates/tools::CutterHand`, right by
  default), separate from the tap's `thread_hand` - a left-hand tap cuts
  a left thread while its spindle may still turn right. The catalog
  reader, the project file, the MCP `tool_edit` and the tool editor
  carry the field; the UI shows a "Left-hand cutter (spindle reverse,
  M4)" row for every kind that turns a spindle.
- The tool gate refuses a left-hand cutter by name for every operation
  whose setup posts through a built-in post that starts a spindle M3 and
  never reverses it (Haas, Tormach PathPilot, Doosan DNM, Grbl 1.1,
  grblHAL, Makera Carvera, Heidenhain, Heidenhain Klartext): at creation
  (`tool_refusal`) and as an operation's after-state (`tool_problem`),
  so generation, the post, the tree and the page all say the same
  sentence. A post that reverses (Fanuc, Mazak, Mach4, Siemens 810M)
  keeps a left-hand cutter offered; a post of the user's own stays open.
- A left-hand cutter rides the generation digest (`stamp_tool`), so a
  tool edited to left-hand marks its operations stale.
- Versions: the project file steps to v83 (a v82 reader would silently
  drop the hand and post M3) and a `.camtools` library with a left-hand
  cutter steps to `CUTTER_HAND_VERSION` 7 (accepted: 1..=7).

Readings: the M3-only list is the maintainer's step-2 list; the
post-side reverse path exists since #988 (`ask_reverse_spindle` + the
`millSpindleReverse` manifest flag), which steps 3 and 4 (#4102) will
read.

Rework (mkinney's review of 8f0cc012, commits 73a142e92 + 98ec365db):
- The law reads the REQUEST, not the post (#4031 rework): a left-hand
  cutter is allowed only for an operation that asks the spindle to
  reverse - today only a Thread operation with spindle reverse, the one
  path that calls `ask_reverse_spindle` and posts M4 - and still
  refused on the M3-only posts even then. A permitted post reverses
  nothing on its own; a user post file is judged by the same request.
  Every other kind - Drill, Face, Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Bore,
  Circular and every multiaxis kind - refuses the left hand by name
  until #4102 lands. A left-hand cutter posts M4 or meets a named
  refusal; it never posts M3.
- Output tests: the Thread op with the ask posts M4 through the Fanuc
  post; the whole catalog table of kinds refuses the left hand without
  the ask; a left-hand Drill refuses at creation and at generation and
  post on the reversing Fanuc as much as on Haas, and no NC file is
  written.
- The example `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` was
  regenerated at v83 through the WRITE_GOLDEN save path. Moved goldens:
  that project file only (its `"version"` row 82 -> 83; the committed
  posted program is byte-identical).
- The library-version boundary test refuses `CUTTER_HAND_VERSION + 1`
  (version 8, the new newest) instead of `TIP_FORM_VERSION + 1`.
- The project file's v83 step is a compatibility break; the ladder
  comment names it and the breaking metadata rides commit 98ec365db.

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/cutter_hand.rs` (new): the tool JSON round trip and
  the unknown-hand refusal; the creation door refuses by name on each of
  the eight M3-only posts; a left-hand Drill refuses even on the
  reversing built-in Fanuc post; a Thread operation that asks to reverse
  posts M4 with the left-hand mill; every kind without the reverse
  request refuses the left hand by name; an edit to left-hand refuses
  generation and post by name (no NC file written); the project round
  trip; the library steps to version 7 only when a left-hand cutter is
  present.
- `crates/tools/tests/cutter_hand.rs` (new): the catalog reader keeps a
  left hand, defaults legacy tools to right, and refuses a bad hand by
  tool and field name. (New top-level test binaries, one per crate,
  because each mirrors an existing issue binary - `tap_hand.rs` - that
  stays a separate suite.)
- `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs`: the newer-number refusal moved
  past version 7.
- `crates/app/tests/tool_law.rs`, `holder_reference.rs`,
  `continuous_4axis_part.rs`, `tap_hand.rs` and the `crates/motion` and
  `crates/ui` suites that seed the field: green.

Gate on the rework head 98ec365db: `cutter_hand` 7 passed,
`continuous_4axis_part` 10 passed, `holder_reference` 7 passed,
`tool_library` 25 passed, `tool_law` 7 passed, `camcraft-ui --lib`
1,688 passed, clippy `camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Not exercised: steps 3 and 4 (#4102) - the posted-G-code proof of the
allow side is today the Thread op's M4; every other kind refuses. The
plasma, wire, sinker and waterjet posts touch no spindle and read no
hand.

Heavy step (P1 under the safety floor): `app heavy: tool_library`, ok on
the reviewed head 8f0cc012; its diff is untouched by the rework.

Changelog: A tool states its cutter hand; a left-hand cutter posts M4
only where the operation asks to reverse, and is refused by name
everywhere else - never posted under M3.

Screenshots:
- Before (the new-tool draft, no hand row):
  https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr4103-tool-hand-before.png
- After (the "Left-hand cutter (spindle reverse, M4)" row, 4x crop):
  https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/blob/pr-screenshots/pr4103-tool-hand-after.png

Fixes #4031

title: refactor(ui): tool drawing inks are theme tokens
body:
The four PRs under this one (#3990, #3992, #3993, #4072) are merged. The branch merges `main` at 498382c8e (5b9256022). The change is 5d2c2b2d6. The review fix is 25b220b34.

## What changed

The fourth family of #1120: the tool drawing inks.

- Eighteen colour tokens join `Tokens`. Each is also a theme-file key (`colors.<name>`):
  - the tool, holder and profile previews: `tool_ground`, `tool_axis`, `tool_grid`, `tool_flute`, `tool_shank`, `tool_body`, `tool_edge`, `tool_holder`, `tool_note`, `tool_dim`;
  - the library thumbnails: `thumb_flute` (their shank reads `tool_shank`);
  - the refusal and warning inks of the tool pages: `bad_ink`, `warn_ink`;
  - the tool body page: `mount_axis`, `mount_radial`, `mount_tip`, `mount_origin`, `mount_hint`.
- Both tables hold the old values, so no pixel changes. The previews keep their own dark ground in the light theme, as before.
- The module colour consts (`NOTE`, `BAD`, `HOLDER`, `BG`, `BODY`, `EDGE`, `DIM`, `WARN`, `CUT`, `SHANK`) become functions with the same visibility (`note_ink()`, `bad_ink()`, `holder_ink()`, `tool_ground()`, ...). Each reads the live token. The callers change by name only. One colour role is one key: the note grey was a const in five files, the axis line in three.
- `theme::with_alpha(colour, alpha)`: a token's own colour at an alpha, read unmultiplied, so a partly transparent token does not darken twice (the defect of the #3993 review). The holder fills (alpha 90 in the profile, 70 in the preview) use it. `ground_ink::facet_veil` now calls it too.
- Draw sites: `tool_profile_page.rs`, `tool_preview.rs`, `tool_model_view.rs`, `tool_body_page.rs`, `tool_body_lathe_page.rs`, `tool_holder_picker.rs`, `tool_cutter_page.rs`, `tool_cutter_params.rs`, and `tool_library_dialog/` (`holder_view.rs`, `side_view.rs`, `thumbs.rs`, `assembly_group.rs`, `preview.rs`).
- The colour-literal guard loses the ten rows of the tool family. `theme/tables.rs` goes from 82 to 118.
- The example theme and the colour table of the user guide have the eighteen keys.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1120-tool-inks.md`.

## Review fix (25b220b34)

The tool list thumbnails (`thumbs.rs`) and the holder outline (`holder_view.rs`) keep their built shapes, and the shapes carry theme colours. Before the fix, each cache key held only the tool or holder inputs, so a theme change kept the old colours.

- Each cache key now also holds the inks that its shapes carry:
  - thumbnails: `thumb_flute` and `tool_shank`;
  - holder outline: `tool_axis`, `tool_body`, `tool_edge` and `tool_dim`.
- The holder ground and the labels are painted live each frame, so they are not in the key.
- `build` takes the inks from the key, so the key and the shapes cannot disagree.
- The cache lookup of the holder view moves into `drawing()`, so a unit test can call it without a window.

## Pinning tests

In `crates/ui/tests/theme_files/tool_inks.rs`, a new module of the existing `theme_files` test binary (#3187: no new binary):

- `the_built_in_columns_keep_the_tool_drawing_colours`: both tables carry the old literals.
- `each_tool_drawing_ink_is_a_theme_key`: each key sets its own ink.
- `a_holder_fill_keeps_the_colour_of_its_token`: the built-in holder gives the old fills at alpha 90 and 70, and a `#FF000080` token gives `[255, 0, 0]` at alpha 70, not a darker red.

The review fix, as unit tests of the `camcraft-ui` lib (no new binary):

- `tool_library_dialog::thumbs::tests::a_theme_change_of_the_inks_builds_the_row_drawing_again`
- `tool_library_dialog::holder_view::tests::a_theme_change_of_the_inks_builds_the_holder_outline_again`

Each test draws, checks that the same inks build nothing, changes the inks, checks one new build with the new colours and no old colour, and checks that the next drawing holds. With the inks removed from the cache comparison, both tests are red. The still-frame tests `a_document_row_has_a_cached_drawing_and_its_gauge_length` and `a_still_frame_builds_no_holder_outline` stay green.

Also: `theme_example::example_loads_and_holds_the_dark_defaults`, `theme_files::viewport_inks::the_facet_veil_keeps_the_hover_colour_of_a_semi_transparent_token` (now through `with_alpha`) and `theme_files::colour_literals::no_colour_literal_outside_the_allowed_rows`.

## Screenshots

The tool library window, a tool open in the library editor (the tool preview), and the tool shape window on its Profile, Body and Holder library tabs, in the dark and light theme. The images come from the off-screen renderer (`egui_kittest` with the headless wgpu device, as in `guide_images`), at 1280 x 720. The images are on the images-only `pr-screenshots` branch of the fork, not on this branch.

A pixel comparison of each pair gives 0 different pixels. The images come from 5d2c2b2d6 and its parent, before the merge of main, so that the pair shows this change only.

title: feat(post): Agie Wire EDM posts reentrant line and arc openings
body:
Stacked on #4022. Own commit: `bea85a429` (the one feature commit of this PR). The other commits are merge commits: `c7934501f` and `2f6476301` merge the #4022 branch (now at `87805dcf9`), and `65ec94c5c` merges `origin/main` at `aef12fea6`. Retarget this PR to `main` before #4022 merges.

## Behaviour

- A Wire Contour with the side **Die** on one selected closed DXF chain now posts through the Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision) post. Before this change, the post refused it ("reads a selected DXF chain only for a captured punch").
- The ISO keeps the nominal walls. It starts at the seam and runs counter-clockwise, with `G01`, `G02` and `G03` blocks and incremental `I`/`J` centres. A clockwise drawing is reversed.
- The SBL and SBR are the zero-step die setup of #2957 (`c_die`). Only the stem, the stock and the hole change.
- The control makes the lead, the passes and the separation. CamCraft writes no lead.
- The app reads the placed walls with the code of the inspection export (#3219). That code is now shared in `crates/app/src/operation/agie_opening.rs`. The inspection export keeps its behaviour.
- The ordinary Wire Contour generator and the wire laws still judge the generated kerf before the native post runs.
- New: `crates/post/src/agie/opening.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/opening/walls.rs` (exact distances between lines and arcs), `examples/agie/reentrant-die.{dxf,camscript}`, a user guide section and `docs/decisions/3178-agie-reentrant-opening.md`.

## Rules and refusals

Each rule uses the rough offset of the 20 mm QN2 row (0.245 mm). Each refusal names the rule and its values.

| Rule | Refusal starts with | Control evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Joints and arc centres on the 0.00001 mm grid, equal squared radii at both arc ends | `Native arc radius rule` (both radii) | `RADB` (0.001 mm difference): the control moved the centre by half the difference. `RADA` (0.003 mm): no plotted path, no message. |
| An inside fillet of the plate (a CCW arc of the CCW opening) has a radius larger than 0.245 mm | `Native arc offset rule` (radius, offset) | `FILR` (R0.2): FORMALCHECK passed, but the Main pass left the arc out and cut a sharp corner. The control does not refuse it. CamCraft refuses it. |
| An arc joins its neighbours tangentially; only two straight walls meet at a sharp corner | `Native joint rule` (the point) | `REENT20`: the sharp tooth tips got round R0.245 turns. |
| A sharp inside corner of the plate leaves at most 0.002 mm | `Strict cover rule` (angle, rest) | Same law as the polygon die. |
| Walls that are not neighbours are more than 2 × (corner reach + 0.245) apart | `The walls from … are … mm apart` | Conservative bound. |
| Hole inside, more than 1 mm from each wall; straight entry wall parallel to X or Y; 3 mm lead and 3 mm of wall each side; lead 0.4 mm clear of other walls | hole and entry texts | `REENT20`: straight lead from the hole to the seam. |
| 0.4 mm of stock beyond each wall and arc extremum; 20 mm plate | stock texts | Same as the polygon die. |

"Tangent entry radius larger than the offset" does not apply: CamCraft writes no arc lead.

## Imported on an offline copy of the control's software (2026-11-25)

- `REENT20` (unmodified output of `examples/agie/reentrant-die.camscript`):
  - The ISO and SBL arrived byte for byte. The tree showed `CCB030[0]`.
  - One formal error before TECCUT ("Technologie : te definiëren"). TECCUT row 0199 (Dia 0.25, H20, Ra 0.30) was assigned. The tree showed `CCB030[4]`, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.
  - FORMALCHECK: no errors. Only the two usual warnings.
  - Plot: the Main pass runs counter-clockwise 0.245 mm inside the opening. The fillets became concentric arcs of r − 0.245. The clockwise R4 tongue tip became a concentric `G02` of R4.245. The Main pass ends 1 mm before the seam. The trims run reversed.
- `FILR`, `RADA` and `RADB` are the same job with one hand edit of the ISO each. CamCraft refuses those edits.

## Readings

- Golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/REENT20.ISO`, line by line in `opening_tests.rs`. N0001 is the seam (the foot of the 5 mm lead from X0 Y−7). N0003 is the R2 corner. N0005 and N0009 are the tooth fillets. N0006 to N0008 are the tooth. N0013 and N0017 are the tongue fillets. N0015 is the R4 tongue tip (G02 about X0 Y4). N0022 returns to the seam.
- The CAM path of the example: 25 moves, the wire laws clean, one captured slug of 789.12 mm².

## Screenshots (review item 1)

The renamed visible texts come from the parent PR #4022. This PR adds no UI change: its own commit `bea85a429` changes no file in `crates/ui`. The five before/after pairs of #4022 apply. The images are only on the fork branch `pr-screenshots`, folder `pr-4022/`. Before: `origin/main` 3bb6647f6. After: the #4022 head.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib, `agie::opening_tests` (9 tests): the golden ISO, the clockwise drawing, the entry choice, each refusal with its values.
- `camcraft-app --test agie_native`:

title: fix(post): name the Agie post "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)"
body:
This PR builds on #4003 (issue #3996), which is merged. The branch started on the #4003 branch and then took `git merge origin/main`. The own commits are f6f40a28a and 1b080d420 (the #4022 review fixes); 028530986 is the merge of `main`.

## Decision

The contributor and the maintainer agreed the name on Discord on 25 Nov 2026. The post that writes AgieVision ISO, SBR and SBL job files for the AGIECUT Classic 2S is now "Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision)". Its refusals say "The Agie Wire EDM job requires ...". The record is `docs/decisions/4000-agie-wire-edm-name.md`.

title: feat(multiaxis): the Rotary Flow multi-band and single-helix kernel
body:
﻿## What changed

The picked Rotary Flow guide chains now read as ONE ordered set. The
chain-set law lives in a new `rotary_flow_set` module of the motion
crate; the band loop of `rotary_flow` gains the shared-boundary dedup,
the single-chain lap, the sense normalization, and the set refusals.

- **Multi-band.** Three or more ordered chains machine one band per
  adjacent pair, and the SHARED boundary chain is cut once: band k > 0
  starts at its first interior pass. Band k - 1's last pass already
  walked the shared chain at the same stations, the same push-out and
  the same climb setting, so nothing is lost.
- **Single helical chain.** A lone chain machines the full revolution:
  the kernel synthesizes the second boundary as the chain's own next
  lap, one whole turn on in the unwrap's own theta (`th + TAU`), every
  other coordinate held. The lap takes no whole-turn alignment (it is
  exact by construction). The lap's two edges are the SAME world curve,
  so the closing pass is dropped - the picked chain emits once.
- **Sense normalization.** A chain wound against its pair is walked
  backwards, said in the notes. This supersedes #2824's opposite-sense
  refusal: the feature layer reads a chain's direction from the mesh,
  never from the pick, so the refusal fired on legal picks the user
  could not reverse (the probe on the bar showed the end-face rings
  extracting wound -TAU while the profile rings extract +TAU). The raw
  pairing of two oppositely wound chains twists the band a whole turn;
  the reversal untwists it. Review rework (PR #4018 review, item 1):
  the normalization now runs ONCE over the complete ordered set
  before any band is cut (`normalize_set`), and the SAME normalized
  guide bounds both adjacent bands - never a per-band copy, which
  left the next band's lower boundary at the raw winding and flipped
  the second band's cutting direction without a change to climb.
- **Ring lap guard.** Review rework (item 2): a single guide that
  turns about the axis at one axial station and one radius - a closed
  ring or an open arc of one - is refused by name before a pass is
  generated (`refuse_ring_lap`): its lap reads a positive angular
  width but sweeps no band area, and the pass family would repeat one
  closed cut. A guide that advances in station or in radius sweeps a
  real band and passes.
- **Refusals, all by name.** Chains that meet or cross are refused at
  the shared spot (the exact segment-pair law, Ericson 5.1, at the
  corner-lattice dust). Consecutive bands whose mean developed offsets
  oppose (dot < 0) are refused as a set out of band order. A
  perpendicular turn is not a doubling back: bands may tile around a
  corner. Zero-length, non-finite and duplicate chains keep the #2824
  refusals.

## Geometry readings

- The lap's developed width is exactly `R_ref * TAU` at the chain's own
  outermost radius: `dth = TAU` and `dv = 0` at every matched place, so
  `cross_width` reads one full revolution. The pass count divides it at
  the stepover, and the emitted count is `ceil(width / step)` - the
  closing pass is the picked chain itself.
- The multi-band dedup emits `count_0 + count_k - (k)` passes over k
  bands: band k > 0 takes `count - 1`, and the first interior pass sits
  one stepover or less from the shared boundary, so the coverage never
  opens a gap.
- Refusal readings: the meet test is the exact segment-pair closest
  distance (four endpoint candidates plus the clamped interior solve,
  Ericson 5.1 as the guard cites it); the backtrack test compares the
  mean developed offsets of consecutive pairs and refuses only a
  strictly negative dot.

## Pins

- Motion, `tests/rotary_flow/bands.rs`: three ordered root helices cut
  two bands in 7 passes (4 + 4 - 1) with pairwise-distinct landings;
  one root helix covers the full revolution in 26 passes, the first
  pass winding exactly `TAU`, gouge-free per the station pin; a ring
  that crosses a corner chain refuses at the crossing's own spot.
  Review rework pins: the middle pick reversed holds the direction
  of every pass of every band for BOTH climb settings (aligned
  control and mixed winding, pass by pass); a single closed ring
  refuses the zero-area lap family by name; a single open ring arc
  refuses the same.
- Motion, unit: the lap morph, the meet law with its witness, the
  backtrack law, the pass-count law, the backward walk (twice is the
  identity, the knots stay ascending), the set normalization (mixed
  winding resolved once, the cascade judged against the normalized
  neighbour), the ring lap guard (a ring refuses, a helix and a
  radial arc pass).
- App, `tests/rotary_flow_band.rs`: three ring chains cut two bands,
  the plunge count agrees with the bands' own stated counts, no two
  passes land on one station, the notes state the shared boundary and
  the sense walk.
- App, `tests/rotary_flow_lap.rs` (new file; reason below): one
  meridian chain machines the full revolution in 19 passes, one
  landing per azimuth, lap note stated; the meridian-plus-ring set
  refuses at the shared corner, with no path cached.

## What was not exercised

- The app-level pins run on the turned bar, not a helical screw: the
  app's slicing refuses open meshes, and a closed screw fixture with
  sharp helical edges is its own fixture work. The helical single-chain
  and multi-band coverage is pinned at the motion level on the groove
  fixture (one-turn and three-turn rotors, station and swept-ball
  proofs).
- The heavy lanes are not run (#3556: no PR gets the full heavy lanes;
  this is a P7 under the safety floor, so no targeted heavy step is
  owed). The light lane ran partially green (motion light: lib, the
  adaptive troch twins, app light: pocket_pass_start); its
  all-binaries release build step failed on machine disk during the
  run, not on code - the same build passed clean after a full rebuild
  of the touched crates.
- No example catalog case exercises Rotary Flow, so their outputs
  cannot change; the quick plan still ran all three catalog suites,
  green.
- The quick gate's app prebuild wedged once (#3675) and the app suites
  were run one by one instead: all 20 planned suites green, clippy
  `-D warnings` clean on both touched crates.
- Review rework head (99283bc76, after the merge of main 49bfcaea8):
  the rework gate ran `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` (683
  passed, 0 failed, 22 ignored), `cargo test -p camcraft-motion
  --test rotary_flow` (14 passed, 1 heavy-ignored), `cargo test -p
  camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_band` (7 passed), `cargo test -p
  camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_lap` (2 passed), the three new
  tests by name, and clippy `-D warnings` clean on
  `camcraft-motion --all-targets` and on the touched
  `camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_band` binary. The light lane of
  the first head stands; the rework diff touches only the flow
  kernel and its own pins, and the review re-runs what it needs.
- The crossing between NON-adjacent guides that the review named
  non-blocking (pre-existing on main) is filed as #4032 and stays
  out of this branch.

## File note (#3187)

`crates/app/tests/rotary_flow_lap.rs` is a new top-level test file: the
rotary domain keeps one top-level file per topic, and a second file
holds these laws so `rotary_flow_band.rs` stays under the 400-line
ceiling.

## Changelog

Rotary Flow: three or more ordered guide chains machine one band per
adjacent pair with the shared boundary cut once; a single guide chain
machines the full revolution as its own next lap; the complete set is
wound one way before the bands are cut, so a reversed pick never flips
a band's cutting direction; a single ring guide - closed or an open
arc - is refused by name, its lap sweeps no band area; chains that
meet or cross, and sets out of band order, are refused by name.

Fixes #2829

title: fix(motion): eliminate full-width cuts at ring merges
body:
## Summary

- Collapse interior Clipper lattice micro-steps (`< 5e-5` mm) in `ring_fill::clean_walk` before `share_ends` so segment tangents stay stable on rings and `WALL` loops.
- Extend `ring_fill` with recursive binary sub-levels up to `RING = 16` (`split_band`), `merge_flank_hits` checks in both Inside and Outside order (`level_flanks::full_width_flanks`), dual reach (`tool_r` for ring gaps, `2.0 * tool_r` where flanks fire), and `tail_extension` (`<= 3.5 * tool_r`) to `c`'s boundary.
- Reject boundary `edge_route` chords in `level_order` and `ring_links` (`chord_full_width`) when both `0.9 * r` flanks cut unmachined stock, and walk the full multi-vertex `via` path in `level_order::join`.
- Record design choices in `docs/decisions/3788-ring-merge-waist.md` (clean-room implementation from Held 1991 and existing flanks and keep-down laws).

## Readings (Before -> After)

- `fig8 Outside` (`offset_pass_start`):
  - Before (`baad348f1`): 15 full-width points across 3 Z-levels.
  - After: 0 full-width points; 0 narrow notes; 3 lifts (named); 0 crossings.
- `fig8 Inside` (`offset_pass_start`):
  - Before (`baad348f1`): 10530 wall points; 0 off-wall points; 1 narrow hit at `(35.8393, 159.0963)`.
  - After: 10293 wall points; 0 off-wall full-width points; 0 narrow notes; 0 lifts; 0 crossings.
- `two_lobe_waist` (`one_ring_set::two_lobe_ring_merge_cuts_no_full_width_at_waist`):
  - Before: Outside had 70 off-wall full-width points and 5 narrow notes.
  - After: 0 off-wall full-width points and 0 narrow notes for Outside and Inside.

## Pinning Tests Verified

- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` (passed)
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start -- -D warnings` (passed)
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --lib machining2d` (`292 passed; 0 failed; 22 ignored`, including `machining2d::ring_fill::tests::a_band_with_a_ring_gap_gets_a_fill_and_a_whole_band_none`)
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --test pass_start_levels --test pass_start_engagement --test pocket3d_pass_start` (`pass_start_engagement`: 8 passed; `pass_start_levels`: 20 passed, including `one_ring_set::two_lobe_ring_merge_cuts_no_full_width_at_waist`; `pocket3d_pass_start`: 4 passed)
- `cargo test --release -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start --test flute_reach -- --include-ignored --nocapture` (`flute_reach`: 4 passed; `offset_pass_start`: 21 passed, including `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`, `fig8_inside_offset_names_each_full_width_cut`, `fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing`, `lifts::fig8_start_sides_lift_only_with_a_named_reason`, `lifts::fig8_outside_pass_links_keep_off_the_part_and_enter_on_cut_floor`)

## Not Exercised

Verification ran in software/tests, not on a mill.

title: fix(tools,sim,ui): read corner_r for dovetail cutters
body:
## What changed

Dovetail cutters (`ToolKind::Dovetail`) now read `corner_r` across geometry, verification, stock simulation, and the UI:

- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `Head::Dove` stores `{ cot, corner_r }`. `Undercut::rho` evaluates the corner arc up to `s_tan = c * (1 + sin t)` and the tangent flank above `s_tan`. `Undercut::contact()` returns `(r, corner_r)`.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `undercut::refusal` checks `corner_r` in `[0, diameter / 2]`, `s_tan <= flute_len + NECK_MEETS`, and neck clearance against the rounded flank.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs` and `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`: `head_outline` and `Tool::meridian` emit the rounded corner arc and straight flank.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/`: `Cutter::atoms` emits `Prof::Zone` (`[0, s_tan]`) and `Prof::Dove` (`[s_tan, flute_len]`), or one `Prof::Zone` when the flank top meets `s_tan`. `swept::rho_expanded` and `rotary_geom::shapes` handle `Prof::Zone`. `Frame` moves to `probe_frame.rs` under the 400-line rule.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/`: `SdfTool::Dovetail` and `RevKind::Dove` add `corner: f64`. `field_dove::dove_dist` computes the exact Euclidean SDF of the rounded dovetail head.

body:

title: fix(ui): the tool window's next tool number skips reserved pockets; the full-probe refusal says what to do
body:
## What changed

Three items from the delta safety read of PR #3284 (#2604):

1. **The tool window's next number.** When you add a tool, the window compares the typed number with the number `AddTool` will give, and queues `SetToolNumber` only when they differ. The window used `tool_numbers::next_free`, which ignores the machine's reserved pockets. With T1 reserved for a probe, a typed 1 queued nothing, and the cutter became T2 with no message. A new function, `tool_numbers::next_free_for`, calls the same allocation as `AddTool` (`tool_reservations::allocate`), and the window uses it. Now a typed 1 goes to `SetToolNumber`, which refuses it by name.
2. **Every probe pocket is full.** A new probe is still refused (a probe in an ordinary pocket can break the control's probe macros). The refusal now names the pockets and says what to do:
   `tool 'Probe 2': the probe pockets of <model> (T1) all hold a tool. Delete or renumber the tool in one of these pockets, or reserve one more probe pocket in the machine file`
3. **Plain words.** A refusal names a `tool_setter` reservation as "tool setter", in the app and in the post check of the tool stream. The word "probe" does not change, so the tests and agents that match on it still match.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3667-tool-reservations.md`.

## How tested

- New app tests in `crates/app/tests/tool_reservations.rs`: `next_free_for_a_new_tool_matches_add_tool`, `a_probe_with_every_probe_pocket_full_says_what_to_do`, `a_tool_setter_pocket_is_named_in_plain_words`.
- New UI test `egui_app::tool_number_tests::a_new_tools_typed_number_is_compared_with_the_reserved_aware_allocation`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- `cargo xtask gate quick`: 29 of 29 steps pass.

## Not exercised

The Add tool button in the desktop app was not clicked. The UI test calls the same function that the button calls.

Changelog: The tool window now expects the same tool number that Add tool gives on a machine with reserved pockets, and a full set of probe pockets gets a refusal that says what to do.
Effort: low

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Screenshots

The state is the one that the review asks for. The mounted machine `SHOT VMC` reserves T1 for a probe. In the Tool library, **New tool…** opens the editor. The tool name is `EM-6`, and the user types **Tool number 1**. Then the user clicks **Add tool**.

| Step | Before (merge base `ddee3aed6`) | After (PR head `b206931ab`) |
|---|---|---|
| Tool number 1 typed | ![before typed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/beb89f265ea7c794034dceb9261867f986a9a137/3976/before-1-typed.png) | ![after typed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/beb89f265ea7c794034dceb9261867f986a9a137/3976/after-1-typed.png) |
| After **Add tool** | ![before added](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/beb89f265ea7c794034dceb9261867f986a9a137/3976/before-2-added.png) The tool gets T2. No message tells the user that T1 was not used. Status: `tool EM-6 added (T2)`. | ![after added](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/beb89f265ea7c794034dceb9261867f986a9a137/3976/after-2-added.png) The tool gets T2. The refusal is visible in the Tool library, in Properties and in the status bar: `tool number not set: invalid parameters: tool 'EM-6' (T1): T1 is reserved for probe on SHOT VMC`. |

title: DXF import: MPOLYGON and 3D surface records hidden in a non-drawing section are refused, not dropped
body:
## What changed

The DXF reader skips the sections that carry no geometry (CLASSES, ACDSDATA, THUMBNAILIMAGE) and refuses a file when a drawable record sits in one of them, so nothing is dropped silently. It knows a record is drawable from `ENTITY_KINDS` in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/entities.rs`. That list lacked `MPOLYGON` and the six SURFACE subtypes (`EXTRUDEDSURFACE`, `LOFTEDSURFACE`, `NURBSURFACE`, `PLANESURFACE`, `REVOLVEDSURFACE`, `SWEPTSURFACE`). They are on the list now (46 to 53 names).

`SUN` stays off the list on purpose. It is in the ENTITIES chapter of the DXF Reference, but AutoCAD writes it in OBJECTS (subclass `AcDbSun`, no `AcDbEntity`), and the OBJECTS reader refuses every kind on this list as "graphical entity in OBJECTS". Adding it would refuse real AutoCAD files with sun settings. A comment above the list says so.

## How tested

- New `dxf_classes_section::mpolygon_and_the_surface_kinds_in_a_section_without_geometry_are_refused`: each of the seven kinds in each of the three inert sections is a named refusal. It fails without the change.
- New `dxf_objects_section::a_sun_object_in_objects_stays_inert`: a SUN object in OBJECTS imports the same entities as the file without it.
- All DXF suites pass (`dxf`, `dxf_classes_section`, `dxf_objects_section`, `dxf_inert_sections`, `dxf_refusals`).
- `cargo xtask gate quick` on Windows: 1203 of 1206 steps pass, clippy clean. The three failures do not touch DXF and come from this checkout: `sinumerik_810m_post::air_cut_kit_posts_cleanly_and_matches_committed_kit` (the golden `.mpf` was checked out with CRLF line endings), `catalog_render::catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly` (`rough-finish`: "its file changed", the same line-ending cause) and `egui_app` (the test binary stops with an access violation, a GPU driver crash here).

## Not exercised

No real DXF file with MPOLYGON or a surface record in an inert section was opened; the tests use synthetic records.

Changelog: DXF import refuses a damaged file that hides an MPOLYGON or 3D surface record in a section without geometry, instead of dropping it silently.
Effort: low

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- The Sodick post refuses an open run's skims by name at its rapid
  guard: its manual states no such pass structure, and the generic ISO
  post is the one that cuts, travels and threads anew around each
  boundary.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

Screenshots (images only on the fork's pr-screenshots branch)

- Controls, before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-controls-before.png
- Controls, after (the new Closing overlap row and its help): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-controls-after.png
- Full window, before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-window-before.png
- Full window, after: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr3617-wire-window-after.png

Rework after the safety review (head 795d69e95)

The eight review items of 2026-11-25 are addressed on the same branch:

1. The Centre slit's run-out clearance joins the generation stamp
   (cutting.rs), so an edited or re-stated clearance reads Stale -
   pinned through the edit command and a project reload (wire_stamp).
2. The overlap's ride includes the seam edge's own remainder back to
   the seam: a 100 mm overlap covers exactly 100 mm of arc, forward
   and reversed, and a ride longer than one full lap is refused by
   name (motion tests, both directions, near the perimeter).
3. An open run's skim passes are rethreaded in the air: a travel move
   (a rapid, no wire through it) marks each pass boundary, the wire
   verify judges each pass at its own kerf and its own ends, and the
   generic ISO post cuts, travels and threads anew around it - a new

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
  - A helix inside the uncut core of a tool that is not centre-cutting (review finding on 4bd091166). The core is `plunge_law::CORE` of the tool radius. The wall circle must stand at least that far off the hole axis (`rc >= CORE * r`). The message names the helix radius, the uncut core and the smallest hole that the tool helixes (Ø9 for a Ø6 tool with no leave). A centre-cutting tool keeps the small helix.
- Pass starts at (#3360, from `main`) on a Helical Bore: one helix for each hole has no ring order. Inside and Outside are refused by name at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The Passes tab shows the refusal under the row. Auto is unchanged.
- Bore `entry` (#3828, from `main` by #3832) on a Helical Bore: the helix is the entry of each hole. Plunge, the default, keeps the helix. Ramp and Helix are refused by name (`helical_entry_refusal`), at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The project file and the stamp keep `entry` and `strategy` apart, so a reopened file shows the same refusal.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and on the Lead-in tab main's Entry group, then a hint that the helix is the entry (hover text) and, for a Ramp or Helix entry, a refusal line. The group stays for the helix, so the user can set the entry back to Plunge.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
  - `a_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_of_a_non_centre_cutting_tool_is_refused`: the review's case (Ø6.5, Ø6 tool, 0.4 mm per turn, helix radius 0.25 mm). The NC tool is refused with "1.500 mm uncut core" and "9.000 mm". Ø9 and the issue's Ø11 counterbore still helix with that tool.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_pass_order_by_name`.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_ramp_or_helix_entry_by_name`: Ramp and Helix are refused with "Helical strategy" and the entry name; Plunge keeps the helix.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `a_small_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_is_refused_through_the_operation`: the review's probe through `operation::generate`. The NC tool is refused; the CC tool keeps the small helix with no plunge.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_pass_order_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator both refuse it.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_ramp_or_helix_entry_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator refuse Ramp and Helix; the pair survives the project file; Plunge is not refused; the pass-order refusal is still reached (one Bore arm in `sane.rs`).
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch. `a_helical_bore_keeps_the_entry_group_and_says_the_entry_refusal`: a Ramp entry on the helix shows the refusal line and keeps the Entry combo; Plunge clears the line.
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::a_helical_bore_says_the_pass_start_refusal` (ui lib): Rings take the order; Helical shows the refusal line.

## Gates

Final head 064549362: a merge of `upstream/main` at 498382c8e (no rebase, no force-push). It has hand edits, so it is a DELTA (`git show --remerge-diff 064549362`).

Conflicts with #3832 (Bore entry), both sides kept:
- `crates/app/src/operation/params/holes.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`: the Bore destructure has `strategy`, `pass_start`, `entry` and `picks: _`.
- `holes_page.rs` Lead-in tab: main's `lead_page::bore_entry_group`, then the helical hint and the entry refusal line.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`: `mod bore_strategy;` and `mod bore_entry_group;`.

Hand edits where git merged without a conflict:
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/sane.rs`: the merge gave two `OpParams::Bore` arms. Main's entry arm came first and hid the helical pass-start arm of this branch. They are one arm now: the entry word, then the pass order, then the helical entry.
- `crates/motion/tests/bore_ramp_angle.rs` (from `main`): `strategy: Default::default()` (Rings).
- `crates/app/tests/bore_helical.rs` (this PR): `entry: Default::default()` (Plunge).

Targeted gate on 064549362 (the full quick gate selects about 800 suites for this diff):
- motion: `bore_helix` 10, `bore_pass_start` 4, `bore_ramp_angle` 4, `circular_helix_rings` 4, `equal_steps` 13. All passed.
- app: `bore_helical` 7, `bore_entry` 8, `bore_pass_start` 3, `break_through` 12, `golden_cl` 34, `mcp` 56, `start_exit_shared` 43. All passed.
- ui lib, filter `bore_strategy`, `bore_entry_group`, `pass_start`: 21 passed.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run on this head. On 6932f4022 they gave 104 steps, 1 failed: `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm` (main red, #3886).

**New test binaries (#3187).** `crates/motion/tests/bore_helix.rs` and `crates/app/tests/bore_helical.rs` stay top-level. Main keeps its Bore suites top-level in the same form (`bore_pass_start.rs`, `bore_entry.rs`, `bore_ramp_angle.rs`), and a move would rename the gate steps that the reviews cite. I can move all Bore suites into one directory suite in a follow-up if the maintainer wants it.

## Screenshots

The Bore operation page, rendered by the UI test harness (`egui_kittest`) from a real Bore operation.

| | Rings | Helical |
|---|---|---|
| Passes tab | ![Passes, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-rings.png) | ![Passes, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-helical.png) |
| Heights tab | ![Heights, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-rings.png) | ![Heights, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-helical.png) |

- Passes tab: the Strategy combo shows the two strategies. The Spring pass check shows only for Helical.
- Heights tab: the last Levels row is "Stepdown" for Rings and "Helix pitch" for Helical.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A tool that is not centre-cutting helixes only when the helix clears its uncut core. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.
- The screenshots show the head 4bd091166. The new refusal line under Pass starts at is pinned by the UI test, not by a screenshot.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.

Branch made from `upstream/main` at 2b95e5701. `upstream/main` merged in at 2d98d87be, 6cfc0a6d4, 01e177bf5, 81365c33b and 33597a2fb.

Fixes #2830
